headline: Four topics, one recurring theme: DNA damage and stromal inflammation set what the immune system sees
summary: The month's strongest papers for this lab converge from different directions on the same junction. On the breast side, a PARP1-selective inhibitor in Brca1-null mouse tumors pushes exactly the upstream half of the lab's model (STING signaling, granzyme B positive CD8 T cells) while never measuring MHC class I. On the ovarian side, senescent NF-kB-active fibroblasts in HGSOC supply the epithelial receptor and kinase the lab's stromal model currently lacks: Tenascin-C binding SDC4 and activating ERK. The ecDNA paper hands over a drug-inducible way to make oncogene-bearing micronuclei on demand, which is the substrate for the lab's cytosolic DNA to cGAS-STING axis, yet measures no immune readout at all. The IGF1R paper puts IGFBP3 downstream of an ERalpha-occupied enhancer, the first published precedent for the kind of claim the lab's own fallopian tube preprint leaves open, though with a mutant epithelial receptor rather than wild-type stromal ERalpha. None of the four tests the HLA-E and NKG2A step of the lab's model, which remains the open gap.
cross_links: NF-kB appears as the shared hub in two topics: driving Tenascin-C in senescent HGSOC fibroblasts (Li et al.) and, in the lab's own model, sitting downstream of cGAS-STING in BRCA1-deficient breast epithelium. Whether these are one stromal-epithelial program with two entry points is a testable question.

The PARP inhibitor and ecDNA papers both generate cytosolic DNA (micronuclei) in cancer cells, and both stop short of the immune readout. Combining them, the Pol theta inhibitor RP-2119 is a way to make MYC-positive micronuclei on demand and then score the lab's cGAS-STING, interferon and MHC-I panel.

The ecDNA paper argues homologous recombination is dispensable for ecDNA maintenance, but the evidence is one partial shRNA BRCA2 knockdown, never BRCA1. That negative result cuts against assuming HR deficiency sustains ecDNA, and is weak enough to be worth testing properly in a BRCA1-null background.

IGFBP3 (ERalpha enhancer target, Amzaleg et al.) and Tenascin-C (NF-kB fibroblast target, Li et al.) are both secreted matricellular or binding proteins that relay a stromal or hormonal signal to the epithelium, the same functional slot POSTN occupies in the lab's fallopian tube model.
actions: Request the day-7 bulk RNA-seq (n=3 per arm) from the DSB1559 authors and score the lab's interferon, antigen-presentation and SASP signatures plus H2-K1, H2-D1, B2m, Tap1, Tap2, Nlrc5 and H2-T23 (the mouse HLA-E counterpart). The tumors and the sequencing exist; the MHC-I question was simply never asked.

Score TNC, SDC4 and the senescence sets (GO:0090398, FRIDMAN_SENESCENCE_UP) on the Fib_PI16_C7, Fib_SFRP4_OGN and Fib_POSTN_ESR1hi subtypes in GSE151214, and check the public p65 ChIP-seq (GSE141992) for binding at POSTN, CCL2 and IL6 promoters.

Add IGFBP3 as a readout to the existing Igf1r knockout RNA-seq, and treat the enhancer coordinates chr7:32,720,197-32,720,643 as a template rather than a result: the lab's equivalent question is whether a stromal ERalpha element sits near Igf1.

Consider RP-2119 (Pol theta inhibitor) as a tool compound to generate ecDNA-specific micronuclei, then read out cGAS, STING1, type I interferon, HLA-C and HLA-E, and NK cell killing. The right cell system needs choosing: the paper's lines are colorectal, prostate and gastric, with no breast or ovarian model anywhere.

papers.title: MMEJ repair of breaks at TA repeats maintains ecDNA and cancer fitness
papers.authors: Billing D, Selvaraj M, Kelley ME, et al.

bibliographic.title: MMEJ repair of breaks at TA repeats maintains ecDNA and cancer fitness

reading.one_line_takeaway: Extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) carries intrinsically fragile TA dinucleotide repeats that break during transcription, and cancer cells need FANCM upstream plus Pol theta (POLQ) mediated microhomology-mediated end joining (MMEJ) downstream to keep ecDNA intact, so Pol theta inhibition selectively destabilizes ecDNA.
reading.tldr: ecDNA drives oncogene amplification and therapy resistance in many cancers, but what keeps these acentric circles intact was unclear. Using isogenic cell line pairs in which the same oncogene sits either on ecDNA (double minutes, DM) or in a chromosomal homogeneously staining region (HSR), the authors show that two chemically distinct Pol theta inhibitors deplete MYC positive ecDNA in COLO320DM but not chromosomal MYC in COLO320HSR, while inhibiting DNA-PKcs (NHEJ) or knocking down BRCA2 (homologous recombination) does not (Fig. 1a to 1e). END-seq maps recurrent spontaneous breaks on the ecDNA chromosome 8 amplicon to TA repeats (11 of 20 peaks overlap TA repeats of at least six units, and none of these peaks appear in HSR cells, Fig. 3e,f), and Repair-seq finds no global or locus specific rewiring of repair pathway choice (Fig. 3b,c), so the dependency is substrate specific rather than a pathway shift. FANCM acts upstream to suppress these breaks, ERCC1-ERCC4 cleaves the structures that escape, and Pol theta repairs the resulting breaks (Fig. 4a to 4g). Single-cell whole-genome sequencing shows FANCM loss and Pol theta inhibition drive deletions and duplications at the same fragile TA rich regions, and TA repeats are enriched at ecDNA breakpoints in pan-cancer whole-genome cohorts (P = 0.000892, Fig. 5b to 5g).
reading.research_question: What keeps extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) intact in cancer cells, and is there a DNA repair dependency specific to ecDNA that could be exploited therapeutically?
reading.background: ecDNA are circular, acentric DNA elements that carry amplified oncogenes, are very highly transcribed, and are associated with faster tumour growth, therapy resistance and worse outcomes. Because ecDNA lack centromeres and segregate randomly, and because their circular topology and high transcription differ fundamentally from linear chromosomes, they face structural challenges that chromosomal amplifications do not. Earlier work established that non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) and homologous recombination (HR) contribute to ecDNA formation and to resolving engineered breaks on ecDNA, and a recent study linked ecDNA replication to ATM dependent damage responses involving TOP1 and TOP2B with some MMEJ contribution. What was missing was whether ongoing maintenance of ecDNA copy number, as opposed to its formation, depends on a distinct repair pathway, and whether ecDNA contains specific fragile sequences that create that dependency. This paper fills that gap by identifying TA dinucleotide repeats as the recurrent breakage substrate and MMEJ as the pathway required to repair them.
reading.study_design: Human cancer cell lines, with isogenic ecDNA versus chromosomal amplification pairs as the central comparison: COLO320DM (ATCC CCL-220, MYC on ecDNA) versus COLO320HSR (ATCC CCL-220.1, MYC in a chromosomal homogeneously staining region), and PC3-DM versus PC3-HSR (gifts from the P. Mischel laboratory). Additional ecDNA lines: SNU-16 (ATCC CRL-5974, MYC and FGFR2 on ecDNA, gastric), NCI-H716 (ATCC CCL-251, colorectal), and HeLa clones with DHFR on ecDNA (PD29424h, maintained in 60 nM methotrexate) or in chromosomal HSRs (PD29426a, 40 nM methotrexate). HEK293T (ATCC CRL-3216) was used for lentiviral production. A mouse model of de novo ecDNA formation used adult neural stem cells from Myc(ec/+); Trp53(fl/fl) mice versus Myc(+/+); Trp53(fl/fl) controls, with Adeno-Cre at 1 x 10^12 particles per ml and 3 weeks of culture, to ask whether Pol theta inhibition depletes ecDNA after it has formed. Perturbations: two chemically distinct Pol theta inhibitors (RP-2119, helicase domain, 100 nM; RP-6685, polymerase domain, 10 micromolar), DNA-PKcs inhibitors NU7441 (1 micromolar) and NU7026 (10 micromolar), stable shRNA against BRCA2 exon 16 (validated by olaparib sensitivity at 1 micromolar), CRISPR-Cas9 ribonucleoprotein nucleofection with a triple guide strategy against POLQ, RHNO1, FANCM, ERCC1 and ERCC4 (with AAVS1 or IL25 guides as controls matched for total guide load), and a RHNO1 knockout line. Combination arms used CHK1 inhibitor CCT245737 (750 nM), methotrexate, and low dose FGFR inhibitor infigratinib (6.25 nM). Transcription was inhibited with triptolide (1 micromolar) or the CDK9 inhibitor AZD4573 (200 nM). Readouts: metaphase FISH counts of oncogene positive ecDNA (at least 20 metaphases per replicate, each dot one metaphase), 53BP1 and gamma-H2AX immunofluorescence foci, micronucleus FISH for MYC, centromere and telomere signals, IncuCyte proliferation and growth competition, Repair-seq style amplicon sequencing of CRISPR-Cas9 induced repair outcomes at AAVS1 and MYC, END-seq mapping of spontaneous double-strand breaks, and DLP+ single-cell whole-genome sequencing after sgFANCM (1 month) or RP-2119 (2 months) with parental T0 and vehicle controls. Human tumour analysis used focal amplification junctions from PCAWG, Hartwig, PedPanCan, GLASS and CUGA, with AmpliconArchitect reconstructions of MYC ecDNA from a medulloblastoma and a neuroblastoma. Cohort sample numbers are not stated in the portion of the text that was available.

key_methods.name: Isogenic ecDNA (DM) versus chromosomal HSR cell line pairs with metaphase FISH counting
key_methods.plain_explanation: A double minute (DM) is a small circle of DNA floating free of the chromosomes, and a homogeneously staining region (HSR) is the same stretch of amplified DNA instead inserted as a long tandem array inside a chromosome. Cell line pairs exist in which the same oncogene is amplified to a similar degree in one or the other configuration, so the only major difference is whether the amplified DNA is circular and free or linear and chromosome bound. Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) on metaphase spreads uses a fluorescent DNA probe against the oncogene, and because the chromosomes are spread out at metaphase you can literally count the number of separate fluorescent dots (ecDNA copies) in each cell.
key_methods.how_used: COLO320DM versus COLO320HSR and PC3-DM versus PC3-HSR were the central comparison throughout. MYC positive ecDNA per metaphase was counted after one week of vehicle, RP-6685 or RP-2119 (Fig. 1b), after NU7441 (Fig. 1c), after shBRCA2 versus shCtrl (Fig. 1d) and after sgRHNO1 (Fig. 1e), with at least 20 metaphases per replicate and n = 3 biological replicates, each dot one metaphase. The same readout was applied to DHFR positive ecDNA in HeLa-DM cells before and after methotrexate with or without Pol theta inhibition (Fig. 2e).
key_methods.why_it_matters: This design is what makes the paper's central claim interpretable: a drug that reduces oncogene copy number in the DM line but not in the isogenic HSR line is acting on the extrachromosomal configuration rather than on the oncogene, the cell line background or general proliferation. The caveat is that metaphase FISH only scores cells that reach metaphase, so any treatment that changes mitotic entry or that kills cells with many ecDNA copies could shift the counted distribution without changing per cell ecDNA maintenance, and the authors' significance keys in these panels report asterisks rather than numeric P values.

key_methods.name: Pol theta inhibition with two chemotypes plus genetic perturbation of the MMEJ axis
key_methods.plain_explanation: Pol theta is the enzyme encoded by the gene POLQ. It is a fusion of a helicase like domain and a DNA polymerase domain, and it is the central enzyme of microhomology-mediated end joining (MMEJ), a backup way of sticking broken DNA ends together. Inhibitors can target either domain, so using one of each chemotype tests whether an effect really comes from blocking Pol theta rather than from an off-target activity of one particular molecule. Genetic removal of the gene is an independent check on the drugs.
key_methods.how_used: RP-6685 (polymerase domain, 10 micromolar) and RP-2119 (helicase domain, 100 nM) were used in parallel across ecDNA depletion, DNA damage, micronucleus, proliferation, END-seq and single-cell sequencing experiments. CRISPR-Cas9 sgRNA against POLQ was used in growth competition assays in COLO320DM versus COLO320HSR (Fig. 2c), and RHNO1, which the authors place in the same axis, was deleted both by nucleofection (Fig. 1e) and as a stable knockout line. Comparator perturbations covered the other two pathways: DNA-PKcs inhibitors NU7441 and NU7026 for NHEJ and shBRCA2 for HR.
key_methods.why_it_matters: Two inhibitors hitting different domains, plus sgPOLQ and sgRHNO1, is the main defence against the conclusion being a single compound artefact, and the NHEJ and HR arms are what license the claim that the dependency is specific to MMEJ. Two caveats remain: RP-6685 is used at 10 micromolar, 100 fold above the RP-2119 concentration, which leaves room for off-target activity at the high dose, and the BRCA2 arm is a partial shRNA knockdown rather than a clean HR null, so a negative result there is weak evidence that HR is genuinely dispensable. The inhibitors come from Repare Therapeutics, with which several authors are affiliated.

key_methods.name: END-seq mapping of spontaneous DNA double-strand breaks
key_methods.plain_explanation: END-seq is a sequencing method that captures the physical ends of broken DNA across the whole genome. Cells are embedded and treated so that only genuine double-strand break ends are available, those ends are blunted and ligated to a sequencing adaptor, and the resulting reads pile up at positions where breaks actually occurred. Unlike methods that infer damage from repair protein recruitment, it reports the break itself, and because it does not require inducing breaks it can show where lesions arise spontaneously.
key_methods.how_used: END-seq was run in COLO320DM versus COLO320HSR cells to map spontaneous lesions across the amplified regions on chromosome 8 (a 1.58 Mb window including MYC), chromosome 6 (126 kb) and chromosome 13 (168 kb), in hg19 (Fig. 3d). Coverage was scaled across the chromosome 8 amplicon and peaks were scored for overlap with TA repeats of at least six units: 11 such loci in DM cells and 0 in HSR cells, against a background track of 59 TA elements meeting that threshold (Fig. 3e,f). Motif enrichment was computed at break sites (Fig. 3g) and seven loci (TA1 to TA7) were shown zoomed, with TA1 to TA3 lying in the highly transcribed MYC to PVT1 region (Fig. 3h). END-seq was then repeated after sgFANCM and Pol theta inhibition, normalized to total MYC coverage (Fig. 4g).
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the experiment that turns a pathway dependency into a mechanism by naming the physical substrate, TA repeats, and the isogenic HSR comparison showing zero overlapping peaks is the strongest single piece of evidence that the fragility is a property of the extrachromosomal configuration rather than of the sequence alone. The caveats are important: the Fig. 3 legend states no replicate number and no P values at all, and the Fig. 4g END-seq comparison is explicitly n = 1 biological replicate with 19 TA repeat loci treated as the units for paired t-tests, which is statistics over loci within a single experiment rather than over independent replicates. I could not read the END-seq Methods, so peak calling parameters and the exact TA repeat definition are unverified.

key_methods.name: Repair-seq style amplicon sequencing of CRISPR induced repair outcomes
key_methods.plain_explanation: To ask which repair pathway a cell prefers, you can make a defined cut at a known position with CRISPR-Cas9 and then sequence that spot deeply in many cells. The scars left behind are pathway specific: clean rejoining with small insertions or deletions indicates NHEJ, deletions flanked by short identical sequences (microhomologies) indicate MMEJ, and precise repair from a template indicates homologous recombination. Counting the proportion of each scar type gives a fingerprint of pathway usage.
key_methods.how_used: Breaks were induced at AAVS1 (a neutral safe harbour locus) and at MYC by CRISPR-Cas9 in both COLO320DM and COLO320HSR cells, and outcomes were quantified by amplicon sequencing and classified as HR, NHEJ, MMEJ or unedited (Fig. 3b), with representative MMEJ associated indels shown for both loci (Fig. 3c).
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the paper's key negative control for its own hypothesis, and it is what makes the mechanism specific. If ecDNA bearing cells had simply rewired themselves to use MMEJ globally, or specifically at the MYC locus, their Pol theta dependency would be trivial. Finding no global and no locus specific shift forces the conclusion that the dependency comes from a particular class of lesion, the spontaneous TA repeat break, rather than from a changed pathway preference. One limitation is that engineered Cas9 breaks are blunt and may not resemble the ends produced by cleavage of a cruciform structure, so this assay may be blind to the pathway choice that actually operates at TA repeats.

key_methods.name: DLP+ single-cell whole-genome sequencing with structural variant calling
key_methods.plain_explanation: DLP+ (direct library preparation) is a method for sequencing the entire genome of many individual cells separately rather than averaging across a population. Each cell gets its own library, so you can see rearrangements that exist in only a few cells. Structural variant calling then identifies deletions, duplications and inversions in each cell, and variants found in one sample but not the parental population can be attributed to what was done to that sample.
key_methods.how_used: COLO320DM cells were sequenced after FANCM knockout (sgFANCM, 1 month) or RP-2119 treatment (2 months), alongside parental (T0) and vehicle controls (Fig. 5a). Sample specific structural variant lengths were compared across conditions for deletions, duplications and inversions (Fig. 5b), the proportion of sample specific deletions overlapping END-seq defined fragile regions on the chromosome 8 amplicon was computed (Fig. 5c), individual deletion sizes were mapped against four END-seq enriched TA rich regions (Fig. 5d), and unique small duplications were counted and mapped, with hatched bars marking those having at least one endpoint in a fragile region (Fig. 5e,f). Statistics were one sided Mann-Whitney U tests with boxes at the 25th to 75th percentiles.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This connects the acute biochemical lesion to a lasting genomic consequence, showing that breaks at TA repeats are not just repaired or lethal but actually reshape ecDNA structure, with FANCM loss producing small duplications that Pol theta inhibition does not. The design has a real confounder that the authors do not control: the sgFANCM arm ran for 1 month and the Pol theta inhibitor arm for 2 months, so differences in structural variant burden between those two arms conflate the perturbation with time in culture and with however many population bottlenecks each arm went through. The number of cells sequenced per condition is in the Methods, which I could not read.

key_methods.name: Immunofluorescence damage foci and micronucleus FISH scoring
key_methods.plain_explanation: When a double-strand break occurs, the histone variant H2AX is phosphorylated (the modified form is called gamma-H2AX) and the adaptor protein 53BP1 is recruited, so both appear as bright microscopic dots at break sites and counting dots per nucleus estimates damage load. A micronucleus is a small separate membrane bound package of DNA that forms when chromatin is left out of the main nucleus at division. Combining micronucleus scoring with FISH probes tells you what DNA is inside: an oncogene probe, a centromere probe (marking whole chromosomes) or a telomere probe (marking chromosome ends).
key_methods.how_used: The percentage of cells with more than five colocalized 53BP1 and gamma-H2AX foci was scored in COLO320 and PC3 DM versus HSR pairs with and without Pol theta inhibition (Fig. 1f), and with triptolide or CDK9 inhibitor to test transcription dependence (Fig. 1g). The same readout was used after sgFANCM (Fig. 4a, n = 4, more than 250 cells per sample), sgERCC1 or sgERCC4 (Fig. 4b, n = 4, more than 200 cells per sample), sgFANCM with sgRHNO1 (Fig. 4c, n = 2, more than 250 cells per sample) and with transcription inhibition (Fig. 4f, n = 3). Micronuclei were scored by FISH for MYC, centromere and telomere after Pol theta or DNA-PKcs inhibition and reversine (Fig. 1h to 1j) and after sgFANCM, sgERCC1 or sgERCC4 (Fig. 4d,e, n = 3, more than 250 cells per sample).
key_methods.why_it_matters: These assays supply the cell biological bridge between the repair defect and the loss of ecDNA: Pol theta inhibition does not simply dissolve ecDNA, it drives MYC bearing ecDNA into micronuclei, and the absence of centromere or telomere enrichment in those micronuclei argues the content is specifically ecDNA rather than missegregated whole chromosomes. The transcription inhibitor arms are what tie the damage to transcription. Scoring is microscopy based with a threshold (more than five foci) and the legends report asterisk significance keys without numeric P values, and Fig. 4c rests on n = 2.

key_methods.name: Pan-cancer focal amplification breakpoint analysis with AmpliconArchitect
key_methods.plain_explanation: AmpliconArchitect is a computational tool that takes whole-genome sequencing from a tumour and reconstructs the structure of amplified regions, deciding whether the amplified DNA is most consistent with a circular extrachromosomal element or a linear chromosomal amplification, and where the junctions between segments lie. Pooling these reconstructions across large tumour cohorts lets you ask whether the junction positions share a sequence feature.
key_methods.how_used: Focal amplification junctions were compared for overlap with TA repeats in ecDNA versus non-ecDNA (linear) amplified regions across the PCAWG, Hartwig, PedPanCan, GLASS and CUGA whole-genome datasets, giving enrichment at ecDNA breakpoints with P = 0.000892 by Pearson's chi-squared test (Fig. 5g). Individual AmpliconArchitect reconstructions of MYC ecDNA from a medulloblastoma (Fig. 5h) and a neuroblastoma (Fig. 5i) were shown with a breakpoint junction overlapping a TA repeat highlighted.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the only part of the paper that tests whether the mechanism operates in human tumours rather than in cultured cell lines, so it carries the translational weight of the argument. It is also the weakest link evidentially: it is a cross sectional association between sequence features and junction positions, it cannot show that MMEJ created those junctions, the cohort sizes are not stated in the text available to me, and a chi-squared test on pooled junctions treats junctions rather than tumours as independent units, which can inflate significance. Whether breast or high grade serous ovarian tumours were represented in this analysis is not stated.

key_concepts.plain_definition: ecDNA is DNA that has broken away from the chromosomes and now exists as a separate circular piece inside the nucleus, typically hundreds of thousands to a few million base pairs long and carrying one or more oncogenes. Because it has no centromere, the structure that spindle fibres grab to pull chromosomes apart, ecDNA is distributed to daughter cells randomly rather than evenly, which lets copy number swing up and down quickly and gives tumours a fast way to amplify a growth gene or shed it when a drug is removed. Under the microscope ecDNA appears as paired dots historically called double minutes, hence the DM label in cell line names. In this paper ecDNA is the central object: the authors argue that its circular topology plus very high transcription make it break at specific sequences, creating a repair dependency that chromosomal copies of the same amplified DNA do not have.

key_concepts.term: HSR (homogeneously staining region) and the DM versus HSR comparison
key_concepts.plain_definition: An HSR is the alternative way a cell can amplify a gene: instead of a free circle, the same DNA is present as many copies lined up head to tail inside a chromosome, which under a stain looks like a long uniformly bright stretch. Some cell lines exist as matched pairs where one carries the amplification as ecDNA and the other as an HSR with similar copy number, for example COLO320DM and COLO320HSR. This pairing is the experimental backbone of the paper, because it holds the gene, the copy number and the cell background roughly constant and varies only whether the amplified DNA is circular and free or linear and chromosomal. Every central claim in the paper rests on something happening in the DM line and not in the HSR line.

key_concepts.term: DNA double-strand break repair: NHEJ, HR and MMEJ
key_concepts.plain_definition: A double-strand break is a cut through both strands of the DNA helix, and cells have three main ways to deal with it. Non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) is the fast default: the Ku protein complex caps the two ends, DNA-PKcs (gene PRKDC) coordinates, and the ends are ligated back with little or no change. Homologous recombination (HR) is the accurate route used mainly after DNA replication: the break is chewed back to single-stranded DNA and the identical sister copy is used as a template, requiring BRCA1, BRCA2 and RAD51. Microhomology-mediated end joining (MMEJ, also called alternative end joining or TMEJ) is a third route that searches for very short stretches of matching sequence, typically two to twenty bases, on the two broken ends, pairs them up, and trims away everything in between, so it always leaves a small deletion with a microhomology at the junction. MMEJ is mutagenic by design. The paper's core claim is that ecDNA maintenance depends specifically on MMEJ, not on NHEJ or HR.

POLQ is the human gene, and Pol theta is the protein it encodes. Pol theta is unusual because it is two machines fused into one: a helicase like domain at one end that can unwind and manipulate DNA and strip proteins off DNA ends, and a DNA polymerase domain at the other end that can extend a DNA strand from a very short, poorly matched pairing. That second property is exactly what MMEJ needs, which makes Pol theta the defining enzyme of the pathway. Because tumours lacking BRCA1 or BRCA2 lean on MMEJ to survive, Pol theta inhibitors have been developed as synthetic lethal drugs for homologous recombination deficient cancers and several are in clinical development. This paper uses two Pol theta inhibitors that hit the two different domains, RP-2119 against the helicase domain and RP-6685 against the polymerase domain, and proposes a different indication for them: destabilizing ecDNA regardless of HR status.

key_concepts.term: TA repeats and cruciform (hairpin) DNA structures
key_concepts.plain_definition: A TA repeat is a stretch where the bases thymine and adenine alternate, written as (TA)n where n is the number of repeats. Alternating TA is the weakest and most easily unwound sequence in the genome, and because the sequence reads the same on both strands running in opposite directions it can pop out of the double helix and fold into a four armed cross shaped structure called a cruciform, essentially two hairpins facing each other. Such structures are well documented in bacterial plasmids. Once extruded they are no longer normal double helix, so structure specific nucleases can cut them, turning a fragile sequence into an actual double-strand break. This paper identifies TA repeats of at least six units as the recurrent break sites on ecDNA (11 of 20 END-seq peaks on the chromosome 8 amplicon, Fig. 3e,f), and proposes, without directly demonstrating it, that transcription driven torsional stress on circular ecDNA extrudes cruciforms there.

FANCM is a DNA translocase, an enzyme that moves along DNA and can push branched or knotted DNA structures back into ordinary double helix. It was first described as part of the Fanconi anaemia pathway that handles DNA crosslinks, but more broadly it acts as a housekeeper that resolves awkward secondary structures and stalled replication intermediates before they become breaks. In this paper FANCM is the upstream, preventive tier of a two tier protection system: it suppresses or smooths the transcription induced structures at TA repeats so they are never cleaved. When FANCM is removed, damage foci and MYC positive micronuclei increase (Fig. 4a,d), TA repeat breaks rise on END-seq (Fig. 4g), and single cells accumulate deletions and small duplications at the fragile TA rich regions (Fig. 5b to 5f).

ERCC1 and ERCC4 (the latter also known as XPF) form a two protein complex that acts as molecular scissors with a particular taste: it does not cut ordinary straight DNA but specifically cleaves at junctions where DNA branches or where a single strand flaps out, which is why it is central to nucleotide excision repair and interstrand crosslink repair. In this paper it supplies the cutting step of the proposed mechanism: structures that escape FANCM are cleaved by ERCC1-ERCC4 to create the break. The supporting evidence is that depleting ERCC1 or ERCC4 suppresses the DNA damage and micronuclei otherwise caused by Pol theta inhibition (Fig. 4b,e), which is the logic of an epistasis experiment, removing the enzyme that makes the lesion rescues the phenotype caused by blocking its repair.

A micronucleus is a small extra nucleus-like body in the cytoplasm, formed when a piece of DNA is left behind outside the main nucleus when a cell divides and then gets wrapped in its own fragile membrane. Micronuclei matter for two reasons: they are a visible sign that DNA was missegregated or damaged, and their membranes rupture easily, spilling DNA into the cytoplasm where the sensor cGAS detects it and triggers STING dependent innate immune signalling. In this paper micronuclei are the fate of destabilized ecDNA: Pol theta inhibition increases MYC positive micronuclei in COLO320DM cells without enriching for centromere or telomere signal (Fig. 1i,j), indicating the trapped material is ecDNA rather than whole chromosomes. The authors do not measure cGAS or STING or any immune consequence.

key_concepts.term: Synthetic lethality and context dependent vulnerability
key_concepts.plain_definition: Synthetic lethality describes the situation where losing either of two genes or functions alone is tolerable but losing both together kills the cell, which is how PARP inhibitors are used against BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutant tumours. A related but distinct idea runs through this paper: a drug can clearly act on its molecular target and change the biology, here depleting ecDNA, without by itself hurting cell growth. Pol theta inhibition alone did not affect proliferation, cell cycle distribution or competitive fitness of COLO320DM cells (Fig. 2a to 2c). A fitness cost appeared only when the cells were made to depend on an ecDNA encoded oncogene, by adding CHK1 inhibition, by selecting HeLa-DM cells with methotrexate so they need DHFR on ecDNA, or by adding low dose FGFR inhibitor to SNU-16 cells that carry FGFR2 on ecDNA (Fig. 2e to 2h). This is the basis for the paper's proposed combination strategy rather than Pol theta inhibitor monotherapy.

key_concepts.term: SBS3 and homologous recombination deficiency signatures
key_concepts.plain_definition: When a particular repair pathway is broken, the mutations a tumour accumulates take on a characteristic pattern of base changes in particular sequence contexts, and these patterns are catalogued as single base substitution (SBS) signatures. SBS3 is the signature associated with homologous recombination deficiency, the state of tumours that have lost BRCA1 or BRCA2 function, and its presence is used as evidence that a tumour has been repairing breaks by error prone backup routes. The authors mention in the Discussion that SBS3 has been reported to accumulate in ecDNA, which they read as independent evidence of ongoing repair activity on these elements. This is cited prior work used as supporting context, not new data generated in this paper, and it is the paper's only substantive contact point with homologous recombination deficiency biology.

Panels f and g are immunofluorescence, plotting the percentage of cells with five or more (f) or more than five (g) colocalized 53BP1 and gamma-H2AX foci, with f comparing COLO320 and PC3 DM against HSR lines with and without Pol theta inhibition (mean plus or minus s.e.m., unpaired two tailed t test) and g adding triptolide at 1 micromolar or CDK9 inhibitor at 200 nM, normalized to DMSO (mean plus or minus s.d., one-way ANOVA). figures.key_result: Both Pol theta inhibitors reduced MYC positive ecDNA per metaphase in COLO320DM cells, while chromosomal MYC in COLO320HSR cells was unaffected (Fig. 1a,b). Neither DNA-PKcs inhibition (Fig. 1c) nor BRCA2 knockdown (Fig. 1d) significantly reduced ecDNA, whereas RHNO1 deletion did (Fig. 1e). ecDNA containing cells carried a higher baseline burden of 53BP1 and gamma-H2AX foci, which Pol theta inhibition increased (Fig. 1f), and inhibiting transcription with triptolide or the CDK9 inhibitor reduced this damage (Fig. 1g). Pol theta inhibition increased MYC positive micronuclei in COLO320DM cells, with no enrichment for centromere or telomere signal (Fig. 1i,j). The legend supplies a significance key from P less than 0.05 to P less than 0.0001 but states no numeric P values for any panel.

figures.label: Fig. 2
figures.title: Cells that rely on ecDNA encoded gene dosage are selectively vulnerable to Pol theta inhibition
figures.question: Does depleting ecDNA with a Pol theta inhibitor actually cost cancer cells fitness, and under what conditions?
figures.how_to_read: Panel a is IncuCyte confluency over time for COLO320DM cells under DMSO or either Pol theta inhibitor (n = 3 biological replicates with 3 technical replicates, mean plus or minus s.e.m.). Panel b is cell cycle distribution by FUCCI fluorescent reporter, normalized to DMSO within each phase (n = 2 to 3, mean plus or minus s.d.). Panel c is a growth competition assay reading the ratio of red to green labelled nuclei over time after sgPOLQ in COLO320DM versus COLO320HSR, with H2B-GFP, H2B-mCherry and sgIL25 controls (n at least 3 biological replicates with 3 technical replicates, mean plus or minus s.d.). Panel d is the schematic for the two dependency models: HeLa cells with DHFR on ecDNA selected with methotrexate, and SNU-16 cells with FGFR2 on ecDNA treated with infigratinib. Panel e quantifies DHFR positive ecDNA per metaphase in HeLa-DM before and after methotrexate with or without Pol theta inhibition, each dot one metaphase, by ordinary one-way ANOVA. Panels f to h are proliferation curves (mean plus or minus s.d., n = 3): f is HeLa cells with chromosomal DHFR HSRs in methotrexate, g is HeLa-DM in methotrexate, h is SNU-16 with vehicle, Pol theta inhibitor, low dose FGFR inhibitor or both.
figures.key_result: Pol theta inhibition alone did not detectably affect proliferation (Fig. 2a), cell cycle distribution (Fig. 2b) or competitive fitness (Fig. 2c) of COLO320DM cells, despite depleting ecDNA. Growth defects emerged only when cells were forced to depend on an ecDNA encoded gene: combined with CHK1 inhibition, with methotrexate selection in HeLa-DM cells but not in the HSR counterpart (Fig. 2f,g), or with low dose FGFR inhibition in SNU-16 cells (Fig. 2h). No P values are stated in the legend.

figures.label: Fig. 3
figures.title: ecDNA accumulates endogenous breaks at TA repeats without global DSB repair rewiring
figures.question: Is the Pol theta dependency caused by ecDNA cells rewiring their repair pathway choice, or by ecDNA carrying a specific class of spontaneous lesion?
figures.how_to_read: Panel a lays out the three competing hypotheses being tested: a global shift toward MMEJ, locus specific rewiring at MYC, or ecDNA specific endogenous breaks. Panel b shows pie charts of repair outcome classes (HR, NHEJ, MMEJ, unedited) after CRISPR-Cas9 cuts at AAVS1 and at MYC in COLO320DM versus COLO320HSR, quantified by amplicon sequencing, with representative MMEJ associated indels in panel c. Panel d shows genome browser tracks of normalized END-seq signal (counts per million) in DM versus HSR cells across the amplified regions of chromosome 8 (1.58 Mb including MYC), chromosome 6 (126 kb) and chromosome 13 (168 kb) in hg19. Panel e shows scaled END-seq coverage across the chromosome 8 amplicon with peaks overlapping TA repeats of at least six units marked in red, against a bottom track of all 59 such TA elements. Panel f is the fraction of END-seq peaks overlapping TA repeats versus other sequences in DM and HSR. Panel g is motif enrichment at break sites in DM cells. Panel h zooms on seven TA repeat loci (TA1 to TA7), with TA1 to TA3 located in the highly transcribed MYC to PVT1 region.
figures.key_result: Repair-seq style amplicon sequencing found no global shift and no locus specific shift in repair pathway usage between ecDNA bearing and HSR cells, at either AAVS1 or MYC (Fig. 3b,c), ruling out pathway rewiring as the explanation. END-seq instead identified recurrent spontaneous breaks on the ecDNA chromosome 8 amplicon, with 11 of 20 peaks overlapping TA repeats of at least six units, and 11 such loci in DM cells against 0 in HSR cells (Fig. 3e,f). The same breaks were absent from the isogenic COLO320HSR line. The figure legend states no replicate number, no sample size and no P values for any panel, which is a notable gap for the paper's central mechanistic figure.

figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.title: FANCM and Pol theta mediated MMEJ cooperate to protect ecDNA from transcription induced damage at TA repeats
figures.question: What makes and what resolves the breaks at TA repeats on ecDNA, and do the proposed upstream and downstream factors act in one pathway?
figures.how_to_read: Panels a to c and f score the percentage of COLO320DM cells with more than five colocalized 53BP1 and gamma-H2AX foci per nucleus: a after CRISPR targeting of FANCM versus AAVS1 control with DMSO or either Pol theta inhibitor (n = 4, more than 250 cells per sample, mean plus or minus s.d.), b after deletion of ERCC1, ERCC4 or IL25 control with or without RP-6685 (n = 4, more than 200 cells per sample), c after sgFANCM, sgRHNO1 or both versus sgAAVS1 (n = 2, more than 250 cells per sample), and f in DM versus HSR cells with DMSO, triptolide or CDK9 inhibitor, with and without FANCM depletion (n = 3, one-way ANOVA with multiple comparisons). Panels d and e score MYC positive and MYC negative micronuclei after sgFANCM (d) or sgERCC1 and sgERCC4 (e), with or without RP-6685 (n = 3, more than 250 cells per sample, mean plus or minus s.e.m.). Panel g shows END-seq signal at TA repeat loci on the chromosome 8 ecDNA amplicon in DM versus HSR after sgAAVS1 or sgFANCM with or without Pol theta inhibition, normalized to total MYC coverage, as boxplots over 19 TA repeat break loci from n = 1 biological replicate, by paired two tailed t tests with multiple comparisons. Panel h is the two tiered protection model schematic.
figures.key_result: FANCM loss increased DNA damage foci (Fig. 4a) and MYC positive micronuclei (Fig. 4d), placing it upstream as a preventive factor. Depleting ERCC1 or ERCC4 suppressed the damage and micronuclei caused by Pol theta inhibition (Fig. 4b,e), identifying this nuclease as the source of the break. Inhibiting transcription rescued the damage caused by FANCM loss (Fig. 4f), tying the lesion to transcription. END-seq showed FANCM loss and Pol theta inhibition each increased breaks at TA repeats with additive effects (Fig. 4g). The critical END-seq panel g is explicitly n = 1 biological replicate with statistics computed across 19 loci, and panel c rests on n = 2; no numeric P values are given for panels a to e.

figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.title: TA repeat fragility drives structural rearrangements on ecDNA
figures.question: Do breaks at TA repeats actually reshape ecDNA structure over time, and is there evidence that this happens in human tumours?
figures.how_to_read: Panel a is the schematic of DLP+ single-cell whole-genome sequencing of COLO320DM cells after sgFANCM (1 month) or RP-2119 (2 months), with parental T0 and control samples. Panel b compares sample specific structural variant lengths (deletions, duplications, inversions) across the four conditions, and panel c the proportion of sample specific deletions overlapping END-seq defined fragile regions on the chromosome 8 amplicon, both as boxplots with one sided Mann-Whitney U tests and boxes at the 25th to 75th percentiles. Panel d maps individual deletion sizes across the amplicon, with four END-seq enriched TA rich regions in grey and TA rich loci in blue. Panel e counts unique small duplications per condition, with hatched bars for duplications having at least one endpoint in a fragile region, and panel f maps them across the amplicon. Panel g is the fraction of focal amplification junctions overlapping TA repeats in ecDNA versus non-ecDNA regions across the PCAWG, Hartwig, PedPanCan, GLASS and CUGA cohorts. Panels h and i are AmpliconArchitect reconstructions of MYC ecDNA from a medulloblastoma and a neuroblastoma respectively, each with a breakpoint junction overlapping a TA repeat highlighted.
figures.key_result: FANCM loss and Pol theta inhibition each produced larger deletions in single cells, and FANCM loss additionally produced small duplications, with both classes enriched at the fragile TA rich regions defined by END-seq (Fig. 5b to 5f). In pan-cancer whole-genome data, TA repeats were significantly enriched at ecDNA breakpoint junctions relative to linear amplicon junctions, with P = 0.000892 by Pearson's chi-squared test (Fig. 5g), the only numeric P value stated in the main figure legends. Individual medulloblastoma and neuroblastoma ecDNA reconstructions showed rearrangement junctions overlapping TA repeats (Fig. 5h,i). Cohort sample numbers are not stated.

key_findings.statement: Inhibiting MMEJ depletes ecDNA in cancer cells, while inhibiting NHEJ or homologous recombination does not, so ecDNA maintenance depends specifically on MMEJ.
key_findings.evidence: Two chemically distinct Pol theta inhibitors (RP-6685, polymerase domain, and RP-2119, helicase domain) reduced MYC positive ecDNA per metaphase in COLO320DM but not chromosomal MYC in COLO320HSR (Fig. 1a,b, one-way ANOVA, at least 20 metaphases per replicate, n = 3). The DNA-PKcs inhibitor NU7441 (Fig. 1c) and shBRCA2 (Fig. 1d) did not significantly reduce ecDNA, whereas sgRHNO1 did (Fig. 1e). Reductions were reproduced in PC3-DM, SNU-16 and NCI-H716 cells and in a mouse adult neural stem cell model where Pol theta inhibition depleted ecDNA after Cre induced formation. Growth competition after sgPOLQ provided a genetic arm (Fig. 2c).

key_findings.statement: Spontaneous double-strand breaks on ecDNA occur at TA dinucleotide repeats, and these breaks are absent when the same amplified sequence sits in a chromosomal HSR.
key_findings.evidence: END-seq across the amplified chromosome 8 region found recurrent peaks in COLO320DM, with 11 of 20 peaks overlapping TA repeats of at least six units, 11 such loci in DM against 0 in HSR, against a background of 59 qualifying TA elements, plus motif enrichment at break sites and zoomed views of TA1 to TA7 with TA1 to TA3 in the highly transcribed MYC to PVT1 region (Fig. 3d to 3h). The DM versus HSR contrast is the key control, since it holds sequence constant and varies topology and context.

key_findings.statement: The damage on ecDNA is transcription dependent, and blocking MMEJ drives ecDNA into micronuclei rather than dissolving it.
key_findings.evidence: ecDNA containing cells had elevated baseline 53BP1 and gamma-H2AX foci that Pol theta inhibition increased (Fig. 1f), and triptolide (1 micromolar) or CDK9 inhibitor (200 nM) reduced this damage (Fig. 1g); foci colocalized with MYC FISH signal. Pol theta inhibition increased MYC positive micronuclei without centromere or telomere enrichment (Fig. 1h to 1j), and transcription inhibition also rescued the damage caused by FANCM loss (Fig. 4f). Live imaging showed no ecDNA untethering at 48 hours and only a modest increase at 72 hours, arguing the micronuclear route is not simple untethering.

key_findings.statement: ecDNA bearing cells have not globally or locally rewired their repair pathway choice, so the MMEJ dependency comes from a specific lesion rather than a changed pathway preference.
key_findings.evidence: Amplicon sequencing of CRISPR-Cas9 induced repair outcomes at AAVS1 and at MYC showed no global shift toward MMEJ and no locus specific rewiring at MYC between COLO320DM and COLO320HSR (Fig. 3a to 3c). This is an informative negative result that narrows the mechanism, though engineered blunt Cas9 breaks may not model cruciform cleavage ends.

key_findings.statement: A two tiered system protects ecDNA at TA repeats: FANCM suppresses the transcription induced structures, ERCC1-ERCC4 cleaves those that escape, and Pol theta mediated MMEJ repairs the resulting breaks.
key_findings.evidence: FANCM loss increased damage foci (Fig. 4a) and MYC positive micronuclei (Fig. 4d); ERCC1 or ERCC4 depletion suppressed the damage and micronuclei caused by Pol theta inhibition, an epistasis result placing the nuclease upstream (Fig. 4b,e); transcription inhibition rescued FANCM loss damage (Fig. 4f); END-seq showed FANCM loss and Pol theta inhibition each increased TA repeat breaks with additive effects (Fig. 4g). The END-seq arm is n = 1 biological replicate with statistics over 19 loci, and the sgFANCM plus sgRHNO1 panel is n = 2, so the ordering is better supported by the foci and micronucleus epistasis than by the sequencing.

key_findings.statement: Pol theta inhibition imposes a fitness cost only when cells depend on an ecDNA encoded oncogene, not as monotherapy.
key_findings.evidence: Pol theta inhibition alone did not change proliferation (Fig. 2a), cell cycle distribution (Fig. 2b) or competitive fitness (Fig. 2c) of COLO320DM cells despite depleting ecDNA. Growth defects appeared with CHK1 inhibition, with methotrexate selection in HeLa-DM cells carrying DHFR on ecDNA but not in the HSR counterpart (Fig. 2e to 2g), and with low dose infigratinib in SNU-16 cells carrying FGFR2 on ecDNA (Fig. 2h). This dissociation between target engagement and fitness is the basis for the proposed combination strategy.

key_findings.statement: Breaks at TA repeats reshape ecDNA structure, producing deletions and, after FANCM loss, small duplications at the fragile sites.
key_findings.evidence: DLP+ single-cell whole-genome sequencing of COLO320DM showed larger sample specific deletions after both sgFANCM and RP-2119, with deletions enriched at END-seq defined fragile regions, and unique small duplications enriched after sgFANCM but not in control or Pol theta inhibitor samples (Fig. 5b to 5f, one sided Mann-Whitney U tests). A design confounder is that the sgFANCM arm ran 1 month and the inhibitor arm 2 months, so cross arm comparisons conflate perturbation with time in culture.

key_findings.statement: TA repeats are enriched at ecDNA rearrangement breakpoints in human tumours, suggesting the mechanism operates in vivo.
key_findings.evidence: Focal amplification junctions from PCAWG, Hartwig, PedPanCan, GLASS and CUGA showed TA repeat enrichment at ecDNA breakpoints relative to non-ecDNA amplicons, P = 0.000892 by Pearson's chi-squared test (Fig. 5g), with AmpliconArchitect reconstructions of MYC ecDNA from a medulloblastoma and a neuroblastoma showing junctions overlapping TA repeats (Fig. 5h,i). This is cross sectional sequence association, not demonstration that MMEJ produced those junctions, and cohort sizes are not stated.

limitations: No breast or ovarian model is used anywhere in the paper. The cell lines are colorectal (COLO320DM, COLO320HSR, NCI-H716), prostate (PC3-DM, PC3-HSR), gastric (SNU-16) and cervical (HeLa clones), plus mouse adult neural stem cells. Whether breast or high grade serous ovarian tumours are represented in the pan-cancer cohorts analysed in Fig. 5g is not stated in the text available to me, and the two individual tumour reconstructions shown are a medulloblastoma and a neuroblastoma (Fig. 5h,i).

The central mechanistic sequencing panel is underpowered. Fig. 4g, the END-seq comparison that establishes additivity between FANCM loss and Pol theta inhibition at TA repeats, is explicitly n = 1 biological replicate, with paired t tests computed across 19 TA repeat loci. Treating loci within a single experiment as independent replicates is pseudoreplication and cannot support a claim about reproducibility across experiments. Fig. 4c rests on n = 2 per condition.

Figure 3, which carries the TA repeat discovery, states no replicate number, no sample size and no P values at all in its legend. The 11 of 20 peak overlap and the 11 versus 0 DM against HSR contrast are therefore reported without any statistical framing or indication of how many END-seq experiments they rest on.

Across Figs. 1, 2 and 4 the legends provide asterisk significance keys but no numeric P values, so effect sizes and their precision cannot be independently assessed from the legends. The only numeric P value in the main figure legends is P = 0.000892 in Fig. 5g.

The two Pol theta inhibitors are used at very different concentrations, RP-2119 at 100 nM and RP-6685 at 10 micromolar, a 100 fold difference. Agreement between two chemotypes is a genuine strength, but a 10 micromolar exposure leaves substantial room for off-target activity, and the paper's own Discussion acknowledges that inhibitor based and synthetic lethality approaches limit the ability to distinguish compensatory pathways.

The conclusion that homologous recombination is dispensable for ecDNA maintenance rests on a partial shRNA knockdown of BRCA2 (Fig. 1d), validated only by olaparib sensitivity, not on a clean HR null background and not on BRCA1 at all. A negative result from incomplete knockdown is weak evidence for dispensability, and residual BRCA2 could be sufficient. This matters for anyone reading the paper as a statement about HR deficient tumours.

ecDNA quantification relies on metaphase FISH, which scores only cells that successfully reach metaphase. Any treatment that alters mitotic entry, mitotic duration or the survival of cells carrying high ecDNA loads could shift the counted distribution without changing per cell ecDNA maintenance. Reversine and nocodazole appear among the reagents, indicating mitotic manipulation in at least some arms.

The DLP+ experiment compares arms of unequal duration, sgFANCM for 1 month against RP-2119 for 2 months (Fig. 5a). Differences in structural variant burden or class between those two arms therefore conflate the perturbation with twice the time in culture and however many population bottlenecks each arm underwent, which is a plausible alternative explanation for the duplication class appearing only after FANCM loss.

The human tumour analysis in Fig. 5g is a cross sectional association between sequence features and junction positions. It cannot show that MMEJ generated those junctions, cohort sample numbers are not stated, and a Pearson chi-squared test on pooled junctions treats individual junctions rather than tumours as independent units, which can inflate significance when junction counts vary widely between samples.

Central mechanistic steps remain models rather than demonstrations, as the authors themselves flag. Cruciform extrusion at TA repeats on ecDNA is proposed by analogy to plasmid literature and is not directly observed; the proposed role of torsional stress and R-loop trapped negative supercoiling is explicitly speculative; the reasons HR and NHEJ fail at these particular ends are offered as alternative hypotheses; and whether the breaks persist into mitosis versus being repaired in S to G2 is unresolved, with the authors stating they cannot rule out an S to G2 contribution.

Substantial conflict of interest around the central reagents. The Pol theta inhibitors RP-2119 and RP-6685 come from Repare Therapeutics; the corresponding author Agnel Sfeir was a co-founder, consultant and shareholder of Repare, and five co-authors (Mathieu, Poirier, Morris, Zimmermann, Zinda) are former Repare employees. The paper's main translational claim is that these compounds have a new indication, so independent replication with non-Repare tool compounds or clean genetic POLQ loss would strengthen it.

Micronucleus formation is shown but its downstream consequences are not tested. Given that micronuclei are a canonical trigger of cytosolic DNA sensing, the absence of any cGAS, STING1, IRF3, NF-kB, interferon or immune readout leaves the immunological consequence of drug induced ecDNA micronucleation entirely open.

Reading limitation on my side: the second half of the Methods was not retrievable, so I could not verify the metaphase FISH and immunofluorescence scoring criteria, the Repair-seq pipeline, END-seq peak calling and the operational definition of a TA repeat, the number of cells sequenced per DLP+ condition and the structural variant calling parameters, the AmpliconArchitect settings, the tumour cohort sizes, or the Statistics and reproducibility section. No Extended Data figure legend was retrievable either, so the controls and supporting results in Extended Data Figs. 1 to 10 are unassessed here.
open_questions: Does the TA repeat and MMEJ dependency hold in breast and ovarian cancer models carrying ecDNA, and are TA repeats enriched at ecDNA breakpoints specifically in breast, triple negative breast and high grade serous ovarian tumours rather than only in the pooled pan-cancer analysis?

What happens in cells that are both ecDNA positive and homologous recombination deficient? Pol theta inhibitors were developed as synthetic lethal agents against BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutant tumours, and this paper gives them a second, HR independent rationale, but the two contexts are never combined experimentally.

Do the MYC positive micronuclei generated by Pol theta inhibition rupture and activate cGAS and STING1, and does that produce type I interferon signalling, altered MHC class I presentation or changed NK and CD8 T cell recognition? The paper creates exactly the substrate for this question but does not address it.

Is cruciform extrusion at TA repeats on ecDNA directly observable, and is the proposed torsional stress mechanism correct? This is the key untested link in the model, and it is what would explain why the same TA sequences are fragile on a circle but not in a chromosomal HSR.

When during the cell cycle are these breaks repaired? The authors invoke RHINO (RHNO1) and its reported mitotic role to suggest TA repeat breaks may persist into M phase, but state they cannot rule out an S to G2 contribution of MMEJ.

Is TA repeat fragility purely a liability, or does it also drive adaptive ecDNA plasticity and heterogeneity over longer timescales, as the authors speculate? If MMEJ both preserves ecDNA short term and diversifies it long term, inhibiting it could have opposing consequences depending on treatment duration.

Does Pol theta inhibition deplete ecDNA and impair fitness in vivo, in animal models or patient derived systems? All fitness data here are from cultured cell lines, and no in vivo or clinical testing is reported.
reading.relevance_to_lab: This paper sits squarely on the lab's extrachromosomal DNA topic and is worth a close read, but its connection to the lab's breast and ovarian work is structural rather than direct, and it is important to be precise about which parts actually touch the lab's model. What connects strongly: ecDNA biology itself, with MYC as the ecDNA borne oncogene throughout, the DM versus HSR isogenic comparison as a clean way to separate circular from chromosomal amplification, ecDNA as a driver of therapy resistance (the HeLa DHFR with methotrexate and SNU-16 FGFR2 with infigratinib experiments in Fig. 2 are direct models of resistance through ecDNA encoded gene dosage, analogous to the lab's interest in PARP inhibitor, platinum and HER2 therapy resistance), and the detection and analysis toolkit the lab lists as of interest, specifically AmpliconArchitect reconstructions (Fig. 5h,i), single-cell whole-genome sequencing by DLP+ (Fig. 5a to 5f) and metaphase FISH ecDNA counting, plus END-seq as a method the lab does not currently list but could borrow to ask where breaks occur in BRCA1 deficient mammary epithelium. The micronuclei link is the most intriguing connection to the lab's BRCA1 model: Fig. 1h to 1j shows that Pol theta inhibition drives MYC positive ecDNA into micronuclei without centromere or telomere enrichment, and the lab's working model runs cytosolic DNA to cGAS-STING to NF-kB and IRF3 and type I interferon to MHC class I changes (HLA-C, HLA-E, NKG2A) and suppressed NK surveillance. This paper therefore supplies a pharmacological, ecDNA specific way to generate micronuclei on demand, which is a potentially useful tool for the lab's immune evasion experiments. Crucially though, the paper measures no immune or innate sensing readout at all: there is no cGAS, STING1, IRF3, NF-kB, interferon, MHC or NK data, so it neither supports nor challenges the lab's model on that axis, it only creates the opening. On homologous recombination deficiency and BRCA genes the paper is partly orthogonal and partly challenging. BRCA1 is not studied. BRCA2 appears only as an shRNA knockdown arm (Fig. 1d) which did not significantly reduce ecDNA, and the authors read this, together with the DNA-PKcs inhibitor result, as showing that ecDNA maintenance needs MMEJ specifically rather than HR or NHEJ. For the lab this cuts against any simple assumption that homologous recombination deficiency is what sustains ecDNA in BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutant breast and ovarian tumours, although the evidence is a partial knockdown and should not be over read. The one direct HR deficiency touchpoint is in the Discussion, where the authors cite prior reports that the SBS3 mutational signature, the signature of HR deficiency, accumulates in ecDNA, which they interpret as evidence of ongoing repair activity on these elements; this is cited background, not new data here. The Pol theta inhibitor angle is where the paper is most actionable for the lab. Pol theta inhibitors are already in clinical development as synthetic lethal agents for HR deficient tumours, which is a context the lab cares about for BRCA1 and BRCA2 mutant breast and high grade serous ovarian cancer. This paper reframes them as ecDNA directed agents acting independently of HR status, and shows the fitness effect is context dependent, appearing only under dependence on an ecDNA encoded oncogene (Fig. 2). The obvious question it raises, which the paper does not test, is whether a BRCA1 mutant breast or HGSOC tumour that is also ecDNA positive presents two convergent vulnerabilities to the same drug class; that inference is mine, not the authors'. Against all of this, the main caveat for the lab is tissue relevance: there is no breast or ovarian model anywhere in the paper, the cell lines are colorectal, prostate, gastric and cervical plus mouse neural stem cells, the two tumour examples shown are paediatric brain tumours, and whether breast or ovarian tumours contributed to the pan-cancer enrichment in Fig. 5g is not stated in the text I could read. A concrete follow up for the lab would be to check ecDNA frequency and oncogene content (MYC, CCNE1, ERBB2, KRAS) against TA repeat content at breakpoints in breast, TNBC, HER2 positive and HGSOC amplicons, using the same AmpliconArchitect based approach, and to ask whether BRCA1 status stratifies that.
discussion_questions: The paper argues HR is dispensable for ecDNA maintenance on the basis of an shRNA BRCA2 knockdown that did not significantly reduce ecDNA (Fig. 1d). How much weight should we put on that negative result, and what would it take to test properly in a BRCA1 or BRCA2 null background relevant to our breast and ovarian models? If HR deficiency genuinely does not sustain ecDNA, does that change how we think about ecDNA in BRCA1 mutant tumours?

Pol theta inhibition drives MYC positive ecDNA into micronuclei (Fig. 1h to 1j) but the paper stops there. Is this a tool we should adopt to generate ecDNA specific micronuclei on demand and then read out cGAS-STING, type I interferon, HLA-C and HLA-E, and NK cell killing, which is exactly the axis of our BRCA1 immune evasion model? What would the right cell system be, given that the paper's lines are colorectal, prostate and gastric?

The central mechanistic END-seq panel (Fig. 4g) is n = 1 biological replicate with t tests across 19 loci, and Fig. 3 reports no n or P values at all. Does the foci and micronucleus epistasis (Fig. 4b,e, where ERCC1 or ERCC4 loss rescues Pol theta inhibitor damage) carry the two tiered model on its own, or is the sequencing evidence load bearing in a way that should make us cautious?

The fitness effect of Pol theta inhibition appears only under dependence on an ecDNA encoded oncogene (Fig. 2e to 2h). If we take that seriously, what is the analogous combination in our systems: Pol theta inhibitor plus HER2 directed therapy in ERBB2 amplified breast cancer, or plus platinum or PARP inhibitor in CCNE1 amplified HGSOC? And would ecDNA positivity need to be a selection criterion for such a combination to work?

The TA repeat fragility mechanism is proposed to arise from circular topology plus high transcription, since the same sequences do not break in the chromosomal HSR (Fig. 3e,f). Given that our interest is in early lesions, would we expect this fragility and its MMEJ dependency to be present in ecDNA in pre-neoplastic breast or fallopian tube tissue, or only once transcription of the amplified oncogene is high?

nodes.label: Two tiered protection: FANCM upstream, Pol theta downstream
nodes.detail: FANCM prevents or resolves transcription induced structures at TA sequences before ERCC1-ERCC4 can cleave them, and Pol theta mediated MMEJ repairs the breaks that escape, with TA fragility also driving ongoing ecDNA rearrangement.

nodes.label: Pol theta inhibition as an ecDNA directed combination strategy
nodes.detail: Because Pol theta inhibition destabilizes ecDNA without intrinsic toxicity, the authors propose combining it with therapies that increase reliance on ecDNA encoded oncogenes, to destabilize ecDNA and counter resistance. No in vivo or clinical testing is reported.

entities.name: ecDNA (extrachromosomal DNA)
entities.description: Acentric circular DNA carrying amplified oncogenes, the central object of the paper and the element whose maintenance is shown to require MMEJ.

entities.name: POLQ
entities.description: Encodes Pol theta, the helicase-polymerase fusion enzyme that defines MMEJ; its inhibition or deletion depletes ecDNA.

entities.name: MMEJ (microhomology-mediated end joining)
entities.description: Mutagenic backup double-strand break repair pathway using short microhomologies, shown here to be specifically required for ecDNA maintenance.

entities.name: FANCM
entities.description: DNA translocase acting as the upstream tier that suppresses transcription induced secondary structures at TA repeats on ecDNA.

entities.name: ERCC1
entities.description: Partner of ERCC4 in a structure specific endonuclease; its depletion rescues Pol theta inhibitor induced damage, placing it as the source of the break.

entities.name: ERCC4
entities.description: Nuclease subunit (also called XPF) that with ERCC1 cleaves the extruded structures at TA repeats that escape FANCM.

entities.name: MYC
entities.description: The oncogene carried on ecDNA in COLO320DM and in a chromosomal HSR in COLO320HSR, used as the FISH readout throughout.

entities.name: TA dinucleotide repeats
entities.description: Alternating T and A sequences of at least six units identified as the recurrent spontaneous break sites on ecDNA and as enriched at ecDNA breakpoints in tumours.

entities.name: NHEJ (non-homologous end joining)
entities.description: Default end joining pathway; inhibiting it with DNA-PKcs inhibitors did not deplete ecDNA, arguing it is dispensable for ecDNA maintenance.

entities.name: Homologous recombination
entities.description: Template based accurate repair pathway; BRCA2 knockdown did not significantly reduce ecDNA, which the authors read as dispensability for maintenance.

entities.name: PRKDC
entities.description: Encodes DNA-PKcs, the NHEJ kinase targeted by NU7441 and NU7026 as the NHEJ comparator arm.

entities.name: BRCA2
entities.description: HR factor knocked down by shRNA as the HR comparator arm; the knockdown was validated by olaparib sensitivity and did not significantly reduce ecDNA.

entities.name: RHNO1
entities.description: Encodes RHINO, placed by the authors in the MMEJ axis; its deletion reduced ecDNA, and its reported mitotic role underpins their speculation about when breaks are repaired.

entities.name: Micronuclei
entities.description: Small extranuclear DNA bodies; Pol theta inhibition drives MYC positive ecDNA into micronuclei without centromere or telomere enrichment.

entities.name: DHFR
entities.description: Gene carried on ecDNA in the HeLa-DM clone, used with methotrexate selection to create dependence on an ecDNA encoded gene.

entities.name: FGFR2
entities.description: Receptor tyrosine kinase gene amplified on ecDNA in SNU-16 cells, used with low dose infigratinib to create ecDNA dependence.

entities.name: COLO320DM
entities.description: Colorectal cancer line carrying MYC on ecDNA (ATCC CCL-220), the primary model for every central experiment.

entities.name: COLO320HSR
entities.description: Isogenic counterpart carrying MYC in a chromosomal homogeneously staining region (ATCC CCL-220.1), the key negative control throughout.

entities.name: RP-2119
entities.description: Pol theta helicase domain inhibitor from Repare Therapeutics, used at 100 nM to deplete ecDNA and in the 2 month single-cell sequencing arm.

entities.name: RP-6685
entities.description: Pol theta polymerase domain inhibitor used at 10 micromolar, the second chemotype that controls against single compound artefacts.

entities.name: Infigratinib
entities.description: FGFR inhibitor used at low dose (6.25 nM) in SNU-16 cells to impose dependence on ecDNA encoded FGFR2 and reveal a Pol theta inhibitor fitness cost.

entities.name: END-seq
entities.description: Genome wide mapping of double-strand break ends, used to localize spontaneous ecDNA breaks to TA repeats and to test FANCM and Pol theta effects.

entities.name: DLP+ single-cell whole-genome sequencing
entities.description: Per cell whole-genome sequencing used to call sample specific deletions, duplications and inversions on ecDNA after FANCM loss or Pol theta inhibition.

entities.name: AmpliconArchitect
entities.description: Computational reconstruction of focal amplifications that classifies them as ecDNA or linear and locates junctions, used for the pan-cancer and individual tumour analyses.

entities.name: Cruciform DNA structure
entities.description: Four armed extruded DNA structure proposed, by analogy to plasmid literature, to form at TA repeats on ecDNA and to be the substrate for nuclease cleavage; proposed rather than directly observed.

entities.name: Transcription
entities.description: High transcription of ecDNA is proposed to generate the torsional stress behind TA repeat structure formation; inhibiting it with triptolide or a CDK9 inhibitor reduces ecDNA damage.

entities.name: ecDNA loss
entities.description: Progressive reduction in oncogene positive ecDNA copies per metaphase, the primary phenotype scored by FISH after repair pathway perturbation.

entities.name: DNA damage on ecDNA
entities.description: Elevated colocalized 53BP1 and gamma-H2AX foci in ecDNA bearing cells, transcription dependent and increased by Pol theta inhibition or FANCM loss.

entities.name: TA repeat double-strand breaks
entities.description: Recurrent spontaneous breaks at TA repeats on the ecDNA amplicon detected by END-seq and absent from the isogenic chromosomal HSR.

entities.name: ecDNA structural rearrangement
entities.description: Deletions and small duplications arising on ecDNA at fragile TA rich regions, seen in single cells after FANCM loss or Pol theta inhibition and at tumour ecDNA breakpoints.

entities.name: Cancer cell fitness
entities.description: Proliferation and competitive growth; reduced by Pol theta inhibition only when cells depend on an ecDNA encoded oncogene, not as monotherapy.

entities.name: HSR (homogeneously staining region)
entities.description: Chromosomal tandem array form of gene amplification, the comparison state in which the same amplified sequence shows no TA repeat breakage and no Pol theta dependency.

entities.name: SBS3 mutational signature
entities.description: Single base substitution signature of homologous recombination deficiency, cited in the Discussion as accumulating in ecDNA and read as evidence of ongoing repair; cited background, not new data here.

entities.name: Pan-cancer focal amplification WGS cohorts
entities.description: PCAWG, Hartwig, PedPanCan, GLASS and CUGA whole-genome datasets used to test TA repeat enrichment at ecDNA versus linear amplicon junctions; sample numbers not stated.

entities.name: Colorectal cancer
entities.description: Tissue of origin of COLO320DM, COLO320HSR and NCI-H716, the main disease context of the cell line work; no breast or ovarian model is used in the paper.
