papers.title: PARP1-selective inhibitor DSB1559 demonstrates superior efficacy and antitumor immunity in triple-negative breast cancer
papers.authors: Nelson A, Zheng KF, Wanderley CWS, Michaud DE, et al.

bibliographic.title: PARP1-selective inhibitor DSB1559 demonstrates superior efficacy and antitumor immunity in triple-negative breast cancer

reading.one_line_takeaway: A PARP1-selective inhibitor, DSB1559, beats olaparib on survival in a Brca1-deficient mouse TNBC model at a 17-fold lower dose, and its advantage tracks with stronger STING signaling, more granzyme B positive CD8 T cells and, uniquely, more mature intratumoral dendritic cells.
reading.tldr: Approved PARP inhibitors such as olaparib hit several PARP family members, and PARP2 inhibition is blamed for much of the hematologic toxicity that limits dosing and combinations. The authors characterize DSB1559, a PARP1-selective inhibitor (2000-fold over PARP2 by NanoBRET, 850-fold by reporter displacement, versus 0.9-fold and 0.6-fold for olaparib), and test it in immunocompetent FVB/n mice bearing orthotopically transplanted Brca1fl/fl Trp53fl/fl mammary tumors. At 3 mg/kg once daily by oral gavage, DSB1559 matched olaparib at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally for PAR inhibition but produced tumor regression and significantly longer overall survival (Fig. 2D,E), with no benefit in BRCA1 add-back tumors (Fig. 2H). Flow cytometry at day 7 showed more CD45+ cells, CD8+ and granzyme B+CD8+ T cells, granzyme B+ NK cells and, only for DSB1559, more cDC1 and cDC2 carrying CD80, CD86 and CD40 (Figs. 3, 5); CD8 depletion blunted efficacy while anti-PD-1 added nothing (Fig. 3K,L). Both drugs also recruited suppressive tumor-associated macrophages (Fig. 4), which the authors propose as the reason anti-PD-1 fails and as the next combination target.
reading.research_question: Does selectively inhibiting PARP1, rather than inhibiting PARP1 and PARP2 together as approved PARP inhibitors do, retain or improve antitumor efficacy in BRCA1-deficient triple-negative breast cancer, and does it reshape the tumor immune microenvironment differently from olaparib?
reading.background: PARP inhibitors (olaparib, talazoparib) are standard of care for germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative breast cancer, but grade 3 or higher adverse events occur in roughly 25% of patients in the adjuvant setting and roughly 38% in metastatic disease, most often anemia and neutropenia, which caps dosing and blocks combinations. Approved PARP inhibitors are not selective: they engage PARP2 and other family members. Preclinical work had suggested that PARP1 inhibition alone is sufficient for synthetic lethality in homologous recombination deficient cells, while PARP2 inhibition drives hematologic toxicity, which motivated PARP1-selective agents such as AZD5305 (saruparib). Separately, PARP inhibitor efficacy had been shown to require cGAS-STING signaling, type I interferon and CD8+ T cells, and PARP inhibitors were known to recruit immunosuppressive tumor-associated macrophages whose removal improves response. The gap this paper fills is whether a more PARP1-selective inhibitor changes that immune response qualitatively, not just the toxicity profile, and whether PARP1 selectivity can be pushed well beyond AZD5305.
reading.study_design: Three layers. (1) In vitro pharmacology: PARP family target engagement by NanoBRET in HEK293 cells and by a reporter displacement assay (n=4 per group), human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell viability over 5 days (n=3 donors), 7-day CellTiter-Glo and colony formation in BRCA2-deficient DLD-1, DLD-1 wild type and BRCA1-deficient MDA-MB-436, plus PARP1 trapping, PARylation and gammaH2AX readouts. Murine KB1P-G3 (Brca1-deficient) versus KB1P-BRCA1 add-back and BRCA wild-type CT26 were used for viability, IFN-beta secretion at 24 h and 72 h, and phospho-STING. (2) ADME and pharmacokinetics: microsomal and hepatocyte intrinsic clearance, plasma stability, protein binding, CYP inhibition, Caco-2 and MDCK-MDR1 permeability; female BALB/c mouse PK at 1 mg/kg intravenous or 10 mg/kg oral; tumor versus plasma exposure in MDA-MB-436 xenografts in NOD-SCID mice after 5 days of 1 to 10 mg/kg DSB1559 or 10 mg/kg AZD5305 (n=3, sampled 1, 4 and 24 h post final dose); rat striatal microdialysis after a single 10 mg/kg oral dose of DSB1559 or niraparib (n=4). (3) Immunocompetent efficacy and immunophenotyping: Brca1fl/fl Trp53fl/fl FVB/n females given intraductal Ad5CMVCre (10 uL, 2.5e7 PFU) to generate tumors, which were banked and implanted as chunks into the fourth mammary fat pad of 6 to 8 week old female FVB/n recipients, randomized at 80 to 200 mm3. Arms: vehicle DMSO intraperitoneally, olaparib 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally daily, DSB1559 3 mg/kg oral gavage daily. Efficacy and survival over 60 days (n=11 to 12 per group); pharmacodynamic IHC and flow cytometry after 7 days (n=5 for IHC, n=7 to 8 for flow); bulk RNA-seq at day 7 (n=3 per group); 45-day antibody studies with anti-CD8 (YTS 169.4), anti-PD-1 (RMP1-14) or IgG isotype (2A3), all 0.2 mg per mouse intraperitoneally twice weekly, with olaparib given at 100 mg/kg oral gavage in these arms (n=5 to 6 per group). A Brca1-deficient 904 versus 904-BRCA1 add-back pair tested target dependence over 21 days (n=5 per group).

key_methods.name: NanoBRET target engagement and reporter displacement assays for PARP family selectivity
key_methods.plain_explanation: Both assays measure how tightly a drug binds a specific protein, and they are run in parallel against each member of the PARP enzyme family. NanoBRET works inside living cells: the target protein is fused to a light-emitting enzyme and a fluorescent tracer is bound to its active site, so when the drug displaces the tracer the light signal changes in proportion to how much drug is bound. The reporter displacement assay is the same logic with purified protein instead of cells. Running both gives an in-cell and a biochemical estimate of the same thing, so a selectivity claim does not rest on one assay format.
key_methods.how_used: DSB1559, AZD5305 and olaparib were profiled against PARP1, PARP2 and other PARP family members, n=4 per group, with results summarized in Fig. 1B and the individual curves in supplemental Fig. S1A to S1L. Selectivity was reported as the PARP1 versus PARP2 potency ratio.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the entire basis of the paper's central premise that DSB1559 is PARP1-selective: 2000-fold by NanoBRET and 850-fold by reporter displacement, against 0.9-fold and 0.6-fold for olaparib and 180-fold and 60-fold for AZD5305. The caveat is that the two formats disagree by more than twofold for DSB1559 and threefold for AZD5305, so the absolute selectivity number is assay dependent, and biochemical selectivity does not by itself prove that PARP2 is spared at the doses used in mice, which was not directly measured in tumor tissue.

key_methods.name: Genetically engineered Brca1fl/fl Trp53fl/fl mouse mammary tumor model, orthotopically transplanted into immunocompetent FVB/n hosts
key_methods.plain_explanation: Brca1 and Trp53 are flanked by loxP sites, short DNA tags that the Cre enzyme recognizes and cuts. Injecting a Cre-carrying adenovirus into the nipple duct deletes both genes in a patch of mammary epithelium, and tumors that resemble human BRCA1-associated triple-negative breast cancer grow from those cells. Those primary tumors are banked and then transplanted as small tissue pieces into the mammary fat pad of normal mice of the same inbred strain, so every recipient has a fully intact immune system and the tumors are genetically matched to the host.
key_methods.how_used: Female Brca1fl/fl p53fl/fl FVB/n mice received 10 uL Ad5CMVCre at 2.5e7 PFU intraductally; resulting tumor chunks were implanted into the fourth mammary fat pad of 6 to 8 week old female FVB/n mice, randomized at 80 to 200 mm3, with tumor volume computed as length times width squared divided by two. Arms were vehicle, olaparib 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally daily and DSB1559 3 mg/kg oral gavage daily (Fig. 2D to G, Figs. 3 to 6).
key_methods.why_it_matters: An immunocompetent, autochthonous-origin, Brca1-null tumor is what makes the immune readouts interpretable at all: the xenograft work in NOD-SCID mice (Fig. 1E, supplemental Fig. S5) cannot show T cell or dendritic cell effects. The caveats are that transplanted chunks bypass the natural initiation and immunoediting of a primary tumor, that a single banked tumor line limits genetic diversity, and that the model does not form CNS metastases, which the authors acknowledge undercuts the clinical framing of the brain penetrance data.

key_methods.name: Pharmacodynamic dose matching by PAR and gammaH2AX immunohistochemistry
key_methods.plain_explanation: PARP1 attaches chains of ADP-ribose (PAR) onto proteins at DNA damage sites, so staining tumor sections for PAR reports how much PARP enzymatic activity is left after dosing: the drug is working if PAR goes down. gammaH2AX is a phosphorylated form of a histone that accumulates at DNA double-strand breaks, so staining for it reports how much unrepaired DNA damage the drug caused. Comparing two drugs at doses that suppress PAR equally is a way to ask whether one produces more damage per unit of target inhibition.
key_methods.how_used: Tumor-bearing mice were treated 7 days with vehicle, olaparib 50 mg/kg or DSB1559 3 mg/kg (n=5 per group), and tumors were stained and quantified for PAR and gammaH2AX (Fig. 2B,C). The 2.94 mg/kg DSB1559 dose was itself chosen from the PARylation IC50 ratio measured in MDA-MB-436 cells relative to olaparib (Fig. 2A).
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the control that makes the efficacy comparison fair rather than a dose artifact: at matched PAR inhibition DSB1559 still caused more gammaH2AX and more tumor regression, which supports a genuine potency or retention advantage rather than simply more drug. The caveat is that dose matching rests on one pharmacodynamic marker at one time point, and plasma exposure of DSB1559 was about 10-fold lower than olaparib (Fig. 2G), so trough target coverage over the dosing interval was not shown to be equivalent.

key_methods.name: Multiparameter flow cytometry immunophenotyping of the day-7 tumor microenvironment
key_methods.plain_explanation: Tumors are dissociated into single cells, stained with a panel of fluorescent antibodies against surface and intracellular proteins, and run through a flow cytometer that records the marker combination on each cell. Cells are then assigned to populations by gating on marker combinations, for example CD11c+CD11b- MHCII+ for type 1 conventional dendritic cells, and populations are reported as a percentage of live cells or as the fraction of a population expressing an activation marker.
key_methods.how_used: Day-7 tumors from vehicle, olaparib 50 mg/kg and DSB1559 3 mg/kg arms (n=7 to 8 per group) were profiled for CD45+ leukocytes, CD3+, CD8+ and granzyme B+CD8+ T cells, CD4+FOXP3- and granzyme B+CD4+ T cells, CD4+FOXP3+ Tregs, PD-1, CD19+CD3- B cells, NKp46+CD3- NK cells and granzyme B+ NK cells (Fig. 3), CD11b+ myeloid cells and CD11b+F4/80+ macrophages with MHCII, CD80, CD86, CD36, PD-L1, CD115 and OPN (Fig. 4), and cDC1, cDC2 with CD80, CD86, CD40 and CCR2 (Fig. 5). Data were analyzed in OMIQ with one-way ANOVA and Fisher's LSD multiple comparisons.
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the only direct evidence that the two drugs differ immunologically rather than just in potency, and the dendritic cell difference (Fig. 5) is the paper's most distinctive claim. The caveats are substantial: the Methods do not state the staining panel or gating strategy (the population definitions appear only in the figure legends), percentages are reported as fractions of live cells so a change can reflect tumor cell killing rather than immune cell influx, and because DSB1559 shrank tumors more than olaparib the composition shift is confounded with differential tumor regression at the same time point.

key_methods.name: Bulk RNA sequencing with GSEA, STRING clustering and mMCP-counter deconvolution
key_methods.plain_explanation: All messenger RNA from a whole tumor is sequenced, giving an average expression level per gene across every cell type present. Genes whose levels differ between treatment groups are identified, then three downstream analyses are applied: gene set enrichment analysis asks whether predefined gene collections such as the Hallmark or Gene Ontology biological process sets are shifted as a group, STRING builds a network of known protein-protein interactions among the changed genes and clusters it to name the processes involved, and mMCP-counter estimates how much of each immune cell type is present from signature genes, which is called deconvolution because it tries to pull cell-type composition back out of a mixed signal.
key_methods.how_used: Day-7 tumors, n=3 per group, RIN above 8.0, Kapa mRNA HyperPrep libraries on an Illumina NovaSeq X Plus, processed through the Dana-Farber VIPER pipeline. DSB1559 versus olaparib gave 414 differentially expressed genes (260 up, 154 down; Fig. 6A,B). GSEA v4.3.2 with Mouse MSigDB v2024.1.Mm and GO biological process both returned immune response enrichment (Fig. 6C,D, top 15 pathways each); STRING v12.0 at minimum interaction score 0.7 with k-means gave three immune clusters, two tied to granzyme-mediated cytotoxicity (Fig. 6E); mMCP-counter via TIMER2.0 (breast invasive carcinoma setting) showed increased T cell and macrophage estimates (Fig. 6F).
key_methods.why_it_matters: It provides an orthogonal, unbiased confirmation of the flow cytometry, and the granzyme clusters line up with the granzyme B protein data in Fig. 3D. The authors themselves flag n=3 as a limitation for GSEA and deconvolution, and two further caveats apply: the specific enriched pathway names are never stated in the text, and mMCP-counter signatures were built for a different context, so a bulk composition estimate from three tumors per arm is suggestive rather than quantitative.

key_methods.name: In vivo immune cell depletion and checkpoint blockade
key_methods.plain_explanation: To test whether a cell type is required for a drug to work, mice are given an antibody that binds a marker on that cell and causes its removal from circulation and tissue, here anti-CD8 for cytotoxic T cells, while control mice get a non-targeting antibody of the same class. The mirror experiment adds an antibody that blocks an inhibitory receptor, here PD-1, to test whether releasing that brake improves the drug's effect.
key_methods.how_used: 45-day survival study with anti-CD8 (clone YTS 169.4), anti-PD-1 (clone RMP1-14) or IgG isotype (clone 2A3), each 0.2 mg per mouse intraperitoneally twice weekly, alone and combined with DSB1559 3 mg/kg oral gavage or olaparib 100 mg/kg oral gavage, n=5 to 6 per group, analyzed by Kaplan-Meier (Fig. 3K,L; supplemental Fig. S9A,B).
key_methods.why_it_matters: The CD8 depletion result is the paper's only causal immune evidence: DSB1559 efficacy depends on CD8+ T cells, not just correlates with them. Two caveats matter. The olaparib comparator switches to 100 mg/kg oral gavage in these arms while the efficacy and immunophenotyping studies used 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally, so the drug arms are not identical across figures, and the Fig. 3K,L legend states one-way ANOVA while the Methods specify log-rank for survival, leaving the test actually applied to the survival curves ambiguous. n=5 to 6 and a single reported experiment also limit the negative anti-PD-1 result.

key_concepts.plain_definition: PARP1 and PARP2 are enzymes that detect single-strand breaks in DNA and respond by building chains of ADP-ribose on themselves and nearby proteins, which recruits the repair machinery. They are two members of a larger PARP family that shares the same catalytic pocket, which is why small molecules aimed at it tend to hit several members at once. Selectivity means the ratio of potency against the intended member versus the others: a 2000-fold PARP1 over PARP2 ratio means it takes 2000 times more drug to inhibit PARP2 than PARP1. In this paper selectivity is the whole point, because the therapeutic effect in BRCA1-deficient tumors is attributed to PARP1 while much of the dose-limiting blood toxicity is attributed to PARP2, so separating the two should widen the therapeutic window. Olaparib is essentially non-selective here (0.9-fold and 0.6-fold), AZD5305 is intermediate (180-fold and 60-fold) and DSB1559 is the most selective (2000-fold and 850-fold).

key_concepts.term: Homologous recombination deficiency and synthetic lethality
key_concepts.plain_definition: Homologous recombination is the accurate way a cell repairs a double-strand DNA break, copying the missing sequence from the matching chromosome; BRCA1 and BRCA2 are required for it. A cell that has lost BRCA1 or BRCA2 is homologous recombination deficient and must fall back on error-prone repair. Synthetic lethality is the situation where losing either one of two genes is survivable but losing both kills the cell: here, blocking PARP1 on top of pre-existing BRCA1 loss leaves the cell unable to handle its own replication-associated damage, so it dies while a BRCA1-intact cell nearby survives. This is why the paper's add-back controls matter: DSB1559 killed KB1P-G3 and 904 Brca1-deficient cells and tumors but not their BRCA1 re-expressing counterparts (supplemental Fig. S4A, Fig. 2H), and did little to wild-type DLD-1 or CT26, which is the signature of an on-target synthetic lethal mechanism rather than general cytotoxicity.

PARylation is the act of adding poly(ADP-ribose) chains to proteins; PARP1 PARylates itself as part of repair, and that self-modification is what lets it release from DNA once the job is done. An inhibitor that blocks the catalytic step stops the self-PARylation, so PARP1 stays stuck on the DNA, a state called trapping. A trapped PARP1 is worse for the cell than an absent one, because the stalled complex physically obstructs the replication fork and converts into a double-strand break. The paper shows both halves in MDA-MB-436 cells: DSB1559 suppressed PARylation and trapped PARP1 (supplemental Fig. S2E,F), and PAR staining in tumors is used as the pharmacodynamic marker for dose matching between DSB1559 and olaparib (Fig. 2B,C).

key_concepts.term: cGAS-STING signaling and type I interferon
key_concepts.plain_definition: cGAS is a sensor protein in the cytoplasm that binds double-stranded DNA wherever it should not be, for instance DNA leaking from damaged nuclei or micronuclei. On binding it makes a small signaling molecule that activates STING (gene symbol STING1), which in turn triggers phosphorylation cascades ending in production of type I interferons such as interferon beta. Type I interferon is the alarm cytokine that recruits and matures dendritic cells, raises antigen presentation and licenses cytotoxic lymphocytes, which is how DNA damage inside a tumor cell becomes an immune signal to the outside. This paper connects the two halves of its story through this pathway: DSB1559 raised secreted interferon beta at 24 h and 72 h and raised phospho-STING more than olaparib in Brca1-deficient KB1P-G3 cells, with no effect in BRCA1 add-back cells (supplemental Fig. S4B to D), and the authors attribute the downstream T cell and dendritic cell changes to this.

key_concepts.term: cDC1 and cDC2 conventional dendritic cells
key_concepts.plain_definition: Dendritic cells are the professional messengers of the immune system: they take up fragments of dead or dying cells, carry them to lymph nodes and display them to T cells, which is how a T cell response to a tumor gets started in the first place. Conventional dendritic cells come in two main types distinguished by their transcription factor requirements and surface markers. Type 1 (cDC1, here gated as CD11c+CD11b- MHCII+, dependent on BATF3 and IRF8) is the subset specialized in presenting tumor-derived antigen to CD8+ T cells and is the one usually rate-limiting for antitumor immunity. Type 2 (cDC2, gated as CD11c+CD11b+ MHCII+, associated with IRF4) favors CD4+ T cell priming. Maturation is read from co-stimulatory molecules CD80, CD86 and CD40, the second signal a T cell needs besides antigen. In this paper the cDC1 and cDC2 increase is the one immune change seen with DSB1559 but not olaparib (Fig. 5A to F), and the supporting transcripts include Itgax, Batf3, Irf4, Irf8, Zbtb46, Flt3, Cadm1, Cd83, Cd40, Cd80 and Cd86 (Fig. 5G).

key_concepts.term: Tumor-associated macrophages and their suppressive phenotype
key_concepts.plain_definition: Macrophages are tissue-resident phagocytes that, inside tumors, are often reprogrammed into a state that restrains rather than helps antitumor immunity: they consume and present antigen but also express ligands that switch T cells off, take up lipids to fuel a tolerant metabolic program, and secrete factors that recruit more of their own kind. The paper reads this state from surface markers on CD11b+F4/80+ cells: antigen presentation and co-stimulation (MHCII, CD80, CD86) alongside suppressive markers CD36 (a lipid scavenger receptor), PD-L1 (gene CD274, the ligand that engages PD-1 on T cells), CD115 (CSF1R, the receptor macrophages need for survival and a drug target) and OPN (gene SPP1). Both olaparib and DSB1559 raised all of these (Fig. 4A to D), so the macrophage arm is a shared liability of PARP inhibition rather than a DSB1559 feature, and the authors use it to explain why adding anti-PD-1 failed (Fig. 3L).

key_concepts.term: Granzyme B as a functional readout of cytotoxic cells
key_concepts.plain_definition: Granzyme B (gene GZMB) is a protein-cutting enzyme stored in the granules of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells and NK cells; when such a cell engages a target it injects granzyme B, which triggers the target's death program. Counting cells is therefore not the same as measuring killing capacity, and intracellular granzyme B staining is the standard way to ask whether the lymphocytes present are actually armed. This paper uses it at both levels: granzyme B+CD8+ and granzyme B+ NK cells rose with both drugs and granzyme B+CD4+ cells rose with DSB1559 (Fig. 3D,F,J), and independently the STRING network of genes upregulated by DSB1559 relative to olaparib contained two clusters tied to granzyme-mediated cytotoxicity (Fig. 6E), with several granzyme genes higher under DSB1559 (supplemental Fig. S11D, individual symbols not stated in the text).

key_concepts.term: Unbound brain-to-plasma partition coefficient (KPuu) and blood-brain barrier penetrance
key_concepts.plain_definition: Most drug in blood is stuck to plasma proteins and cannot act, and the same is true in brain tissue, so comparing total concentrations between blood and brain is misleading. KPuu is the ratio of free, unbound drug concentration in brain to free drug concentration in plasma: a value near 1 means the barrier is effectively not restricting the drug, while a value well below 1 means active efflux or poor permeation. It is measured here by microdialysis, a technique that threads a small semipermeable probe into brain tissue (rat striatum) and samples the interstitial fluid directly. DSB1559 was detectable 30 minutes after a single 10 mg/kg oral dose and reached KPuu 0.3 (Fig. 1F), higher than niraparib, which the authors call the most brain-penetrant approved PARP inhibitor, and comparable to AZD9574 (KPuu 0.31). This matters clinically because BRCA-associated breast cancer carries elevated CNS metastasis risk, but the authors concede their mouse model does not form CNS metastases, so no efficacy against brain disease is shown.

key_concepts.term: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell (HSPC) viability as a toxicity surrogate
key_concepts.plain_definition: Hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells are the bone marrow cells that regenerate all blood lineages; they divide rapidly and depend on DNA repair, which is why anemia and neutropenia are the characteristic PARP-inhibitor toxicities. Exposing primary human HSPCs to a drug in culture and measuring how many survive is a cell-level stand-in for that clinical toxicity, cheaper and faster than a mouse blood count but also much further from the patient. DSB1559 and AZD5305 both preserved HSPC viability better than olaparib, including at 10 micromolar, and at higher concentrations DSB1559 preserved it better than AZD5305 (Fig. 1C, n=3 donors). This is the paper's only toxicity evidence: no mouse hematology, bone marrow or blood count data are reported, so the reduced hematologic toxicity claim is an inference from three donors in vitro plus body weight curves (Fig. 2F).

key_findings.statement: DSB1559 is far more PARP1-selective than olaparib and more selective than AZD5305, the benchmark PARP1-selective agent: 2000-fold over PARP2 in cells and 850-fold biochemically, against 0.9-fold and 0.6-fold for olaparib and 180-fold and 60-fold for AZD5305.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 1B selectivity summary with per-target curves in supplemental Fig. S1A to S1L, n=4 per group, by NanoBRET and by reporter displacement assay.

key_findings.statement: In immunocompetent mice bearing Brca1-deficient TNBC, DSB1559 at 3 mg/kg orally produces tumor regression and significantly longer overall survival than olaparib at 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally, despite matched PAR inhibition and roughly 10-fold lower plasma exposure.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 2B,C (matched PAR, higher gammaH2AX, n=5), Fig. 2D,E (60-day growth and Kaplan-Meier survival, n=11 to 12 per group), Fig. 2G (plasma concentration at 1 h, n=7 to 8).

key_findings.statement: The efficacy is BRCA1-dependent and therefore on target: DSB1559 extended survival in Brca1-deficient 904 tumors but not in BRCA1 add-back tumors, and in vitro it killed Brca1-deficient KB1P-G3 but not KB1P-BRCA1 add-back or BRCA wild-type CT26 cells.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 2H (21-day Kaplan-Meier, n=5 per group) and supplemental Fig. S4A; supplemental Fig. S2A,B for the human DLD-1 and MDA-MB-436 panel.

key_findings.statement: DSB1559 efficacy requires CD8+ T cells, whereas adding anti-PD-1 provides no additional benefit over DSB1559 alone, mirroring olaparib.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 3K anti-CD8 depletion (clone YTS 169.4, 0.2 mg per mouse twice weekly) reduced efficacy in a 45-day survival study, n=5 to 6 per group, with supplemental Fig. S9A; Fig. 3L anti-PD-1 (clone RMP1-14) showed no improvement, supplemental Fig. S9B.

key_findings.statement: DSB1559 uniquely increases intratumoral conventional dendritic cells and their maturation, a difference from olaparib at both protein and transcript level, and the authors propose this as a mechanism for its superior efficacy.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 5A to F (cDC1 and cDC2 frequency, CD80/CD86/CD40, CCR2+ subsets, n=7 to 8 per group); Fig. 5G,H (Itgax, Batf3, Irf4, Irf8, Zbtb46, Flt3, Cadm1, Cd83, Cd40, Cd80, Cd86 and chemokines Ccl2 to Ccl5, Xcl1, Ccr2, Ccr5, Ccr7, n=3 per group).

key_findings.statement: DSB1559 engages STING signaling and type I interferon output more strongly than olaparib, and only in BRCA1-deficient cells, which provides the mechanistic bridge from DNA damage to the immune changes.
key_findings.evidence: Supplemental Fig. S4B,C (secreted IFN-beta at 24 h and 72 h in KB1P-G3, higher for DSB1559 at comparable concentrations, absent in KB1P-BRCA1) and supplemental Fig. S4D (phospho-STING); referenced again in the Discussion.

key_findings.statement: Both drugs increase cytotoxic lymphocyte content broadly, including NK cells: CD45+, CD8+, granzyme B+CD8+, NKp46+CD3- NK cells and granzyme B+ NK cells all rose with olaparib and DSB1559, while B cells and PD-1 on CD8+ T cells were unchanged.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 3A,C,D,H,I,J, day-7 flow cytometry, n=7 to 8 per group, one-way ANOVA with multiple comparisons.

key_findings.statement: PARP1 selectivity does not avoid the immunosuppressive macrophage response: DSB1559 raised CD11b+F4/80+ TAMs and their CD36, PD-L1, CD115 (CSF1R) and OPN (SPP1) expression to a similar degree as olaparib, which the authors invoke to explain the failure of PD-1 blockade.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 4A to D, n=7 to 8 per group; interpreted alongside Fig. 3L and prior work that depleting PARP-inhibitor-induced TAMs improves olaparib response.

key_findings.statement: An unbiased transcriptomic comparison supports a stronger immune program under DSB1559 than olaparib, with 414 differentially expressed genes (260 up, 154 down), immune enrichment by GSEA and GO biological process, granzyme-cytotoxicity STRING clusters, and higher mMCP-counter T cell and macrophage estimates.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 6A to F, n=3 per group; supplemental Fig. S10 principal component analysis, supplemental Figs. S11 to S14.

key_findings.statement: DSB1559 spares human hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells better than olaparib and better than AZD5305 at high concentrations, and is brain penetrant with KPuu 0.3 in rat striatum, exceeding niraparib.
key_findings.evidence: Fig. 1C (5-day HSPC viability, n=3 donors, including at 10 micromolar); Fig. 1F (rat striatal microdialysis after a single 10 mg/kg oral dose, n=4 per group).

limitations: Authors' own: group sizes are small, which they flag specifically for the GSEA and mMCP-counter analyses built on n=3 tumors per arm; the flow cytometry arms are n=7 to 8 and the antibody survival arms n=5 to 6, all from what the Fig. 3 legend describes as one experiment.
Authors' own: the tumor microenvironment was analyzed only at day 7, so later adaptive responses, resistance and the immune state at the time survival diverges are unknown.
Authors' own: the Brca1-deficient model does not form CNS metastases, so the brain penetrance data (Fig. 1F, KPuu 0.3) are pharmacokinetic only and no CNS efficacy was tested.

Authors' own: long-term clinical follow-up is needed to confirm that PARP1 selectivity preserves efficacy while improving tolerability, and some studies implicate PARP2 in metastatic progression, so sparing PARP2 might not be purely beneficial.

Methodological: immune populations are reported as percentages of live cells, and DSB1559 shrank tumors more than olaparib at the same day-7 time point, so the composition differences are confounded with differential tumor regression. A reduced tumor cell denominator alone can raise every immune fraction, and no absolute cell counts per gram of tumor are reported.

Methodological: the comparator is not constant across figures. Olaparib is 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally in the efficacy and immunophenotyping studies (Figs. 2 to 6) but 100 mg/kg oral gavage in the antibody studies (Fig. 3K,L), and DSB1559 is always oral. Dose, route and schedule therefore all differ between the two drugs, so olaparib's apparent inferiority could partly reflect suboptimal exposure rather than lower intrinsic activity.

Methodological: dose equivalence rests on a single pharmacodynamic marker (PAR by IHC at day 7, Fig. 2B,C) and on a PARylation IC50 ratio measured in a human cell line (Fig. 2A). Trough target coverage over the dosing interval was not shown, and DSB1559 plasma exposure was about 10-fold lower (Fig. 2G), so matched inhibition at one time point does not establish matched inhibition over 24 h.

Methodological: the Methods do not report the flow cytometry antibody panel or gating strategy; population definitions appear only in the figure legends, and no gating figure content is described, which limits reproducibility of the central immune claims.

Methodological: effect sizes are not reported. Significance appears only as asterisk thresholds, with no exact p-values, confidence intervals, median survival times or hazard ratios anywhere in the text, so the magnitude of the DSB1559 versus olaparib survival advantage cannot be judged. The Fig. 3K,L legend also states one-way ANOVA for survival curves while the Methods specify log-rank, leaving the actual test ambiguous.

Methodological: the mechanistic link from STING to the dendritic cell and T cell phenotype is correlative. Interferon beta and phospho-STING were measured only in cultured cells (supplemental Fig. S4B to D), not in tumors, and no Sting1 or Cgas knockout, STING inhibitor or dendritic cell depletion experiment was done, so the proposed STING-to-cDC1-to-CD8 axis is inferred rather than demonstrated in vivo.

Methodological: the reduced hematologic toxicity claim, which is the whole rationale for PARP1 selectivity, is supported only by 5-day viability of HSPCs from three donors (Fig. 1C) plus body weight curves (Fig. 2F). No mouse complete blood counts, reticulocyte counts or bone marrow analyses are reported, and in vitro HSPC viability is a weak surrogate for clinical anemia and neutropenia.

Methodological: the human cell line work uses only two homologous recombination deficient lines (MDA-MB-436 and DLD-1) with no numeric IC50 values given in the text, and the in vivo work rests on banked tumors from a single genetic model transplanted as chunks, so neither tumor heterogeneity nor patient-level variation is represented.

Interpretation: industry involvement is substantial and should be weighed. Duke Street Bio Ltd, which owns the compound, funded the work; three authors (Michaud, McGuinness, Wise) hold executive roles there and Campbell is an employee; Wise is a co-corresponding author; and the senior author (Guerriero) advises Duke Street Bio. The comparator choice, dosing and the framing of DSB1559 as superior to the published AZD5305 benchmark should be read in that light.

Reporting: several internal inconsistencies exist (olaparib dose and route differing between Methods and figures, the Fig. 5F legend assigning CCR2+ cDC2 where the text emphasizes CCR2+ cDC1, Cd103 written where the MGI symbol is Itgae, statistical test mismatches), which suggests the figure legends and Methods were not fully reconciled.
open_questions: Is the dendritic cell advantage of DSB1559 causally required for its superior survival benefit, or a downstream marker of greater tumor cell death? A cDC1 depletion experiment (for example Batf3 knockout or anti-XCR1) combined with DSB1559 would settle it.

Does the proposed STING dependence hold in vivo? Treating Sting1-deficient or Cgas-deficient hosts, or hosts given a STING inhibitor, would test whether the T cell and dendritic cell changes and the survival benefit actually require the pathway.
Would a head-to-head study at genuinely exposure-matched doses, same route, and with mouse blood counts included, still show DSB1559 beating olaparib on both efficacy and tolerability?
Is the NK cell increase (Fig. 3I,J) functionally relevant, and does PARP1-selective inhibition change MHC class I or the NKG2A ligand HLA-E axis in BRCA1-deficient cells? Neither was measured here.
Since both drugs recruit suppressive TAMs expressing CSF1R and SPP1, does combining DSB1559 with CSF1R blockade or a TLR agonist convert the failed PD-1 combination into a durable response?

Does PARP1-selective inhibition retain efficacy against BRCA1-deficient tumors that have already acquired PARP-inhibitor resistance, and does sparing PARP2 affect metastatic progression as some cited work suggests?
Given KPuu 0.3 but no CNS metastasis model, does DSB1559 or the clinical lead DSB2455 control BRCA1-associated brain metastases in a model that actually forms them?
reading.relevance_to_lab: Directly relevant to the lab's BRCA1 immune evasion model, and useful mainly as a pharmacological test of the upstream half of that model in an immunocompetent setting. The lab's working chain is BRCA1 loss leading to cytosolic DNA, cGAS-STING, NF-kB and IRF3 with type I interferon, then MHC class I changes (HLA-C, HLA-E and NKG2A) and SASP changes, then suppressed NK and CD8 T cell surveillance. This paper takes the same Brca1-null mammary epithelial starting point (Brca1fl/fl Trp53fl/fl FVB/n, intraductal Ad5CMVCre, the same class of model the lab uses) and shows that pharmacologically amplifying the DNA damage input with a PARP1-selective inhibitor pushes the chain forward in the expected direction: more phospho-STING and secreted IFN-beta, strictly dependent on BRCA1 status since KB1P-BRCA1 add-back cells show neither (supplemental Fig. S4B to D); then more CD8+ and granzyme B+CD8+ T cells, more NKp46+ and granzyme B+ NK cells (Fig. 3C,D,I,J), and more mature cDC1 and cDC2 (Fig. 5). The CD8 depletion result (Fig. 3K) and the 904 versus 904-BRCA1 add-back survival comparison (Fig. 2H) are the strongest pieces: they say the therapeutic effect in a Brca1-null mammary tumor is both BRCA1-dependent and T cell dependent, which supports the lab's premise that the immune arm is not incidental to BRCA1-deficient breast cancer biology. Three specific points of friction are worth raising at journal club. First, the paper never measures MHC class I, HLA-C, HLA-E or NKG2A, and does not name interferon or antigen presentation gene sets in its enrichment results (Fig. 6C,D), so it leaves the lab's MHC-I and NK recognition step completely untested even though the model and the readouts were in hand. The RNA-seq data (n=3 per arm, day 7, Brca1-deficient tumors) would be worth requesting from the corresponding authors to score the lab's own interferon, antigen presentation and SASP signatures, and to check H2-K1, H2-D1, B2m, Tap1, Tap2, Nlrc5 and the Qa-1b gene H2-T23, the mouse counterpart of HLA-E. Second, the paper reports NK cell increases but never tests whether NK cells matter, only CD8 cells; a parallel anti-NK1.1 depletion in this model is an obvious and cheap experiment the lab is well placed to interpret. Third, the macrophage result (Fig. 4) adds a mechanism the lab's current model does not include: both drugs recruit TAMs with CD36, PD-L1, CSF1R and SPP1, which could blunt the very NK and CD8 surveillance the lab studies, so an immune evasion model built only on tumor-intrinsic MHC-I and SASP changes may be incomplete for the treated setting. There is also a methodological borrow: the dendritic cell gene panel in Fig. 5G and the chemokine TPM panel in Fig. 5H give a ready-made cDC1 and cDC2 signature set to apply to the lab's mouse bulk RNA-seq, and mMCP-counter via TIMER2.0 (Fig. 6F) is a quick deconvolution to run on the same data. The ecDNA topic connects too, since PARP inhibitor resistance and cytosolic DNA sensing are shared ground, but this paper does not address ecDNA or micronuclei. Caveats to carry: the comparator dosing is inconsistent across figures, immune changes are fractions of live cells in tumors of different sizes, the STING link is cell culture only, and Duke Street Bio, the compound's owner, funded the study with four authors employed there or in executive roles and the senior author advising them.
discussion_questions: The immune differences in Figs. 3 to 5 are percentages of live cells measured at day 7, when DSB1559 tumors are already regressing and olaparib tumors are not. How much of the dendritic cell and T cell advantage could be a denominator effect from greater tumor cell killing, and what would it take to separate the two: absolute counts per gram, an earlier time point before growth curves diverge, or an olaparib dose titrated to match DSB1559's tumor control?

The lab's model predicts MHC class I remodeling (HLA-C, HLA-E, NKG2A) downstream of BRCA1 loss and cGAS-STING, and this study had the right tumors and RNA-seq in hand but never looked. If we obtain their day-7 bulk data (n=3 per arm) and score H2-K1, H2-D1, B2m, Tap1, Tap2, Nlrc5 and H2-T23, what result would support our model and what result would force us to revise it?

NK cells and granzyme B+ NK cells rose with both drugs (Fig. 3I,J), yet only CD8 depletion was tested. Given our focus on NK surveillance in BRCA1-deficient breast tissue, is an anti-NK1.1 depletion arm in this model worth proposing as a collaboration, and would a negative result (no loss of DSB1559 efficacy) weaken our emphasis on NK cells or simply reflect that CD8 cells can compensate in an established tumor?

Both olaparib and DSB1559 recruited suppressive TAMs expressing CD36, PD-L1, CSF1R and SPP1 (Fig. 4), and the authors use this to explain why anti-PD-1 failed (Fig. 3L). Should our BRCA1 immune evasion model incorporate a myeloid arm alongside the tumor-intrinsic MHC-I and SASP changes, and does the TAM response represent a separate evasion route that would also operate during tumor initiation, not just under treatment?

Duke Street Bio funded the work, owns DSB1559, employs four authors including a co-corresponding author, and the senior author advises the company. The comparator olaparib is dosed intraperitoneally at 50 mg/kg in the efficacy studies but orally at 100 mg/kg in the antibody studies, and DSB1559 is always oral. How much does this affect our confidence in the central superiority claim, and which single additional experiment would most reduce that concern?

nodes.label: PARP inhibitor toxicity limits dosing; PARP2 is the suspected cause
nodes.detail: Olaparib and talazoparib are standard of care in germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative breast cancer, but grade 3 or higher events hit roughly 25% of adjuvant and 38% of metastatic patients, mostly anemia and neutropenia. Prior work indicated PARP1 inhibition alone suffices for synthetic lethality while PARP2 inhibition drives the hematologic toxicity.

nodes.label: PARP inhibitor efficacy needs STING and CD8 cells but recruits suppressive TAMs
nodes.detail: Established background: PARP inhibitor response depends on cGAS-STING signaling and type I interferon to mobilize CD8+ T cells, yet PARP inhibitors also recruit immunosuppressive tumor-associated macrophages whose removal improves response.

nodes.label: Does PARP1-selective inhibition keep efficacy and change tumor immunity?
nodes.detail: The gap: whether a highly PARP1-selective inhibitor retains or improves antitumor activity in BRCA1-deficient TNBC, and whether it reshapes the immune microenvironment differently from a broad PARP inhibitor rather than only improving tolerability.

nodes.label: DSB1559 will beat olaparib and induce stronger antitumor immunity
nodes.detail: Hypothesis that a brain-penetrant, highly PARP1-selective inhibitor can exceed olaparib's efficacy at much lower exposure while engaging STING and cytotoxic lymphocytes more strongly and sparing blood progenitors.

nodes.label: Profile PARP family selectivity, HSPC viability, ADME and brain exposure
nodes.detail: NanoBRET in cells plus a biochemical reporter displacement assay across the PARP family (n=4), 5-day human HSPC viability (n=3 donors), in vitro ADME, mouse pharmacokinetics, tumor versus plasma exposure in MDA-MB-436 xenografts, and rat striatal microdialysis (n=4).

nodes.label: Treat immunocompetent Brca1-null mouse TNBC at PAR-matched doses
nodes.detail: Brca1fl/fl Trp53fl/fl FVB/n tumors made by intraductal Ad5CMVCre and transplanted into the fourth mammary fat pad of female FVB/n hosts; DSB1559 3 mg/kg oral daily versus olaparib 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally daily, dose matched by PARylation IC50 and tumor PAR staining, with BRCA1 add-back tumors as the on-target control.

nodes.label: Profile the day-7 immune microenvironment and test CD8 and PD-1 causally
nodes.detail: Day-7 multiparameter flow cytometry (n=7 to 8 per group) for T, NK, B, myeloid and dendritic cell populations plus bulk RNA-seq (n=3 per group) with GSEA, STRING clustering and mMCP-counter, then 45-day survival studies adding anti-CD8 (YTS 169.4) or anti-PD-1 (RMP1-14), n=5 to 6 per group.

nodes.label: 2000-fold PARP1-selective, spares blood progenitors, brain penetrant
nodes.detail: 2000-fold PARP1 over PARP2 by NanoBRET and 850-fold by reporter displacement, against 0.9-fold and 0.6-fold for olaparib and 180-fold and 60-fold for AZD5305. HSPC viability was preserved better than olaparib and, at high concentrations, better than AZD5305, and DSB1559 reached rat striatum by 30 minutes with KPuu 0.3, exceeding niraparib.

nodes.label: Oral 3 mg/kg DSB1559 beats olaparib 50 mg/kg, only when BRCA1 is lost
nodes.detail: At matched PAR inhibition DSB1559 produced more gammaH2AX, tumor regression and significantly better overall survival than olaparib over 60 days (n=11 to 12) despite roughly 10-fold lower plasma exposure, and it extended survival in Brca1-deficient 904 tumors but not in 904-BRCA1 add-back tumors (n=5 per group).

nodes.label: DSB1559 raises phospho-STING and interferon beta more than olaparib
nodes.detail: In Brca1-deficient KB1P-G3 cells DSB1559 increased secreted interferon beta at 24 h and 72 h and phospho-STING more than olaparib at comparable concentrations, with no effect in KB1P-BRCA1 add-back cells. Measured in culture, never in tumors.

nodes.label: More cytotoxic CD8 and NK cells, and CD8 cells are required
nodes.detail: Day-7 flow cytometry: CD45+, CD8+, granzyme B+CD8+, NKp46+CD3- NK and granzyme B+ NK cells rose with both drugs, with CD3+ and granzyme B+CD4+ rising under DSB1559, while B cells and CD8 PD-1 were unchanged. Anti-CD8 depletion reduced DSB1559 efficacy, the paper's only causal immune evidence.

nodes.label: Only DSB1559 increases cDC1, cDC2 and their maturation
nodes.detail: DSB1559 but not olaparib raised cDC1 and cDC2 frequency, CD80, CD86 and CD40 on them, and CCR2+ dendritic cells, with matching transcripts (Itgax, Batf3, Irf4, Irf8, Zbtb46, Flt3, Cadm1, Cd83, Cd40, Cd80, Cd86) and chemokines (Ccl2 to Ccl5, Xcl1, Ccr2, Ccr5, Ccr7).

nodes.label: Both drugs recruit suppressive TAMs and anti-PD-1 adds nothing
nodes.detail: DSB1559 raised CD11b+F4/80+ macrophages and their CD36, PD-L1, CD115 (CSF1R) and OPN (SPP1) as much as olaparib, so PARP1 selectivity did not avoid this liability, and adding anti-PD-1 failed to improve DSB1559 efficacy, matching olaparib.

nodes.label: PARP1-selective inhibition is sufficient and superior in Brca1-null TNBC
nodes.detail: DSB1559 delivers BRCA1-dependent, CD8 T cell dependent antitumor activity exceeding olaparib at a roughly 17-fold lower dose, so PARP2 engagement is not required for efficacy and sparing it may widen the therapeutic window.

nodes.label: Dendritic cell engagement separates PARP1-selective from broad inhibition
nodes.detail: Stronger STING signaling and the dendritic cell recruitment and maturation seen only with DSB1559 are proposed to drive its superior efficacy, and bulk RNA-seq agrees: 414 differentially expressed genes versus olaparib (260 up, 154 down), immune enrichment by GSEA and GO biological process, granzyme-cytotoxicity STRING clusters and higher mMCP-counter T cell and macrophage estimates. The suppressive macrophage response is a shared liability.

nodes.label: Pair PARP1 inhibitors with TAM or STING agents, not PD-1 blockade
nodes.detail: Because suppressive TAMs rise under both drugs while PD-1 blockade fails, the authors propose CSF1R or TAM-directed agents, TLR agonists, STING agonists, PARP7 inhibition or antibody-drug conjugates as rational partners. The brain-penetrant profile (KPuu 0.3) and the related clinical lead DSB2455 in phase Ia or Ib trial NCT06458712 carry the program forward, though no CNS metastasis model was tested.

entities.name: PARP1
entities.description: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1, the single-strand break sensor and the selective target of DSB1559; its inhibition and trapping is held to be sufficient for synthetic lethality in BRCA1-deficient tumors.

entities.name: PARP2
entities.description: Related PARP family member co-inhibited by olaparib; its inhibition is blamed for hematologic toxicity, so DSB1559 was designed to spare it (2000-fold selectivity by NanoBRET).

entities.name: BRCA1
entities.description: Human homologous recombination repair gene; BRCA1-deficient MDA-MB-436 cells and BRCA1 add-back lines define the on-target window for DSB1559 in this paper.

entities.name: Brca1
entities.description: Mouse ortholog deleted with Trp53 by intraductal Ad5CMVCre to generate the FVB/n mammary tumor model used for all immunocompetent efficacy and immune profiling experiments.

entities.name: Trp53
entities.description: Mouse tumor suppressor deleted together with Brca1 in the Brca1fl/fl Trp53fl/fl FVB/n model, required for tumor formation in this system.

entities.name: BRCA2
entities.description: Second homologous recombination gene; BRCA2-deficient DLD-1 cells served as the second sensitive human line, with wild-type DLD-1 as the matched resistant control.

entities.name: DSB1559
entities.description: The PARP1-selective, brain-penetrant inhibitor characterized here; 3 mg/kg oral daily outperformed olaparib 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally on survival in Brca1-deficient mouse TNBC.

entities.name: olaparib
entities.description: Approved non-selective PARP inhibitor used as the comparator throughout, essentially equipotent on PARP1 and PARP2 (0.9-fold and 0.6-fold selectivity).

entities.name: AZD5305 (saruparib)
entities.description: Benchmark PARP1-selective inhibitor used as an in vitro and pharmacokinetic comparator; 180-fold and 60-fold PARP1 selectivity, less than DSB1559.

entities.name: niraparib
entities.description: Approved PARP inhibitor described as the most brain-penetrant of its class, used as the comparator in rat striatal microdialysis where DSB1559 exceeded it.

entities.name: DSB2455
entities.description: Structurally related clinical lead compound from the same program, in a phase Ia or Ib trial (NCT06458712); not tested experimentally in this paper.

entities.name: STING1
entities.description: Innate DNA-sensing adaptor (merged with STING); its phosphorylation rose more with DSB1559 than olaparib in Brca1-deficient KB1P-G3 cells and is the proposed bridge to the immune response.

entities.name: IFNB1
entities.description: Interferon beta, the type I interferon measured as secreted protein at 24 h and 72 h; higher with DSB1559 than olaparib and absent in BRCA1 add-back cells.

entities.name: type I interferon signaling
entities.description: The cGAS-STING output pathway that recruits and matures dendritic cells and licenses cytotoxic lymphocytes; invoked as the mechanism linking DNA damage to the observed immune changes.

entities.name: homologous recombination repair
entities.description: Accurate double-strand break repair pathway requiring BRCA1 and BRCA2; its loss is what makes tumor cells dependent on PARP1 and thus vulnerable to DSB1559.

entities.name: PARylation
entities.description: PARP1-catalyzed addition of poly(ADP-ribose) chains; measured as PAR immunohistochemistry in tumors and used to dose-match DSB1559 3 mg/kg against olaparib 50 mg/kg.

entities.name: synthetic lethality
entities.description: Death of a cell only when two defects coincide, here BRCA1 loss plus PARP1 inhibition; demonstrated by loss of DSB1559 activity in BRCA1 add-back cells and tumors.

entities.name: triple-negative breast cancer
entities.description: The disease modeled, with the lowest survival among breast cancer subtypes and few targeted options; modeled here as Brca1-null Trp53-null mouse mammary tumors in FVB/n hosts.

entities.name: CD8+ T cell
entities.description: Cytotoxic T lymphocyte; increased in frequency and granzyme B content by both drugs, and functionally required for DSB1559 efficacy as shown by antibody depletion.

entities.name: granzyme B+ CD4+ T cell
entities.description: Cytotoxic CD4+ T cell state increased specifically by DSB1559 in day-7 tumors, part of the broader cytotoxic lymphocyte shift.

entities.name: NK cell
entities.description: NKp46+CD3- natural killer cell; both total and granzyme B+ NK cells increased with olaparib and DSB1559, but their functional contribution was never tested by depletion.

entities.name: cDC1
entities.description: Type 1 conventional dendritic cell (CD11c+CD11b- MHCII+), the subset that primes CD8+ T cells against tumor antigen; increased and matured by DSB1559 but not olaparib.

entities.name: cDC2
entities.description: Type 2 conventional dendritic cell (CD11c+CD11b+ MHCII+), favoring CD4+ priming; also increased and matured only by DSB1559.

entities.name: tumor-associated macrophage
entities.description: CD11b+F4/80+ macrophage in a suppressive state (CD36, PD-L1, CD115, OPN high); recruited equally by both drugs and proposed as the reason PD-1 blockade failed.

entities.name: hematopoietic stem and progenitor cell
entities.description: Human blood-forming progenitor used as the in vitro surrogate for PARP inhibitor hematologic toxicity; viability was better preserved by DSB1559 than olaparib.

entities.name: GZMB
entities.description: Granzyme B, the cytotoxic protease used as the functional arming readout in CD8, CD4 and NK cells, and reflected in the granzyme-cytotoxicity STRING clusters.

entities.name: PDCD1
entities.description: PD-1, the T cell inhibitory receptor; unchanged on CD8+ T cells after treatment, and its antibody blockade failed to improve DSB1559 efficacy.

entities.name: CD274
entities.description: PD-L1, the PD-1 ligand; increased on tumor-associated macrophages by both drugs as part of the suppressive phenotype.

entities.name: CSF1R
entities.description: CD115, the macrophage survival receptor raised on TAMs by both drugs; named as a candidate combination target for PARP1-selective inhibitors.

entities.name: SPP1
entities.description: Osteopontin (OPN), raised on tumor-associated macrophages by both drugs and read as part of a lipid-metabolic suppressive program alongside CD36.

entities.name: CCR2
entities.description: Chemokine receptor marking the trafficking dendritic cells increased by DSB1559, and upregulated transcriptionally along with Ccl2 to Ccl5, Xcl1, Ccr5 and Ccr7.

entities.name: BATF3
entities.description: Transcription factor required for cDC1 development; its transcript (Batf3) was among the dendritic cell maturation genes raised by DSB1559 relative to olaparib and vehicle.

entities.name: H2AX
entities.description: Histone whose phosphorylated form gammaH2AX marks DNA double-strand breaks; raised in vitro and in tumors by both drugs, and more by DSB1559 at matched PAR inhibition.

entities.name: brain
entities.description: Target tissue for the microdialysis study; DSB1559 reached rat striatum within 30 minutes with KPuu 0.3, relevant to BRCA-associated CNS metastasis risk but untested for efficacy.

relations.evidence: DSB1559 engages PARP1 with 2000-fold selectivity over PARP2 by NanoBRET and 850-fold by reporter displacement assay, n=4 per group.
PARP2 is inhibited only at far higher concentrations, which is the basis of the selectivity claim; the sparing is relative, not absolute.
Olaparib inhibits PARP1 but with essentially no selectivity over PARP2 (0.9-fold by NanoBRET, 0.6-fold by reporter displacement).
Olaparib is equipotent on PARP2, which the authors tie to its hematologic toxicity profile.
AZD5305 (saruparib) showed 180-fold and 60-fold PARP1 selectivity, intermediate between olaparib and DSB1559.
PARP1 catalyzes poly(ADP-ribose) chain formation; PAR staining in tumors falls when the enzyme is inhibited and was used for dose matching.
DSB1559 3 mg/kg suppressed tumor PAR to the same degree as olaparib 50 mg/kg over 7 days, n=5 per group.
BRCA1 is required for homologous recombination repair; its loss is the basis of the synthetic lethal window exploited here.
BRCA2 is likewise required for homologous recombination; BRCA2-deficient DLD-1 cells were sensitive while wild-type DLD-1 showed limited loss of viability.
DSB1559 reduced viability and formed colonies poorly in BRCA1-deficient MDA-MB-436 and BRCA2-deficient DLD-1 but not wild-type DLD-1, KB1P-BRCA1 add-back or CT26 cells.
DSB1559 induced gammaH2AX in MDA-MB-436 and DLD-1 cells and, at PAR-matched dosing, more gammaH2AX in tumors than olaparib.
DSB1559 increased phospho-STING in Brca1-deficient KB1P-G3 cells more effectively than olaparib, with no effect in KB1P-BRCA1 add-back cells. Measured in culture only.
Secreted interferon beta rose at 24 h and 72 h in KB1P-G3 cells, higher with DSB1559 than olaparib at comparable concentrations and absent in BRCA1 add-back cells.
STING activation drives type I interferon output, the pathway the authors invoke to connect DNA damage to dendritic cell and T cell changes. Cited background, not dissected here.
Type I interferon recruits and matures cDC1; the authors attribute the DSB1559-specific dendritic cell response to stronger STING and interferon signaling, inferred rather than tested in vivo.
DSB1559 but not olaparib increased cDC1 frequency and CD80, CD86, CD40 and CCR2 on them in day-7 tumors, n=7 to 8 per group.
DSB1559 but not olaparib increased cDC2 frequency and their co-stimulatory molecules in day-7 tumors.
Batf3 was among the cDC1-associated maturation and lineage transcripts raised by DSB1559 relative to vehicle and olaparib, n=3 per group.
CCR2+ cDC1 and cDC2 increased under DSB1559, and Ccr2 transcript rose along with Ccl2 to Ccl5, Xcl1, Ccr5 and Ccr7.
CD8+ and granzyme B+CD8+ T cells increased in day-7 tumors with DSB1559 (and with olaparib), reported as a percentage of live cells.
Anti-CD8 depletion (YTS 169.4, 0.2 mg per mouse twice weekly) reduced DSB1559 efficacy in a 45-day survival study, n=5 to 6 per group, showing CD8+ T cells are required for tumor control.
Granzyme B positivity was used to define armed cytotoxic CD8+ T cells, which rose with both drugs, and granzyme-cytotoxicity clusters appeared in the STRING network.
Granzyme B+ CD8, CD4 and NK fractions rose under DSB1559 and several granzyme genes were significantly higher than under olaparib in bulk RNA-seq.
NKp46+CD3- NK cells and granzyme B+ NK cells increased in day-7 tumors with both DSB1559 and olaparib; no NK depletion was performed to test function.
Granzyme B+CD4+ T cells increased specifically after DSB1559 treatment in day-7 tumors.
DSB1559 increased CD11b+ myeloid cells and CD11b+F4/80+ macrophages to a similar extent as olaparib, so PARP1 selectivity did not avoid this response.
Olaparib likewise raised myeloid and macrophage infiltration with the same suppressive marker profile, consistent with prior reports.
PD-L1 was raised on CD11b+F4/80+ macrophages by both drugs as part of the suppressive phenotype.
CD115 (CSF1R) was raised on macrophages by both drugs, and CSF1R-directed TAM targeting is proposed as a combination strategy.
OPN (SPP1) was raised on macrophages by both drugs alongside CD36, read as a lipid-metabolic suppressive program.
The authors propose that PARP-inhibitor-induced suppressive TAMs restrict T cell function, which would explain why anti-PD-1 added no benefit; inferred, not directly tested here.
PD-1 is the inhibitory receptor on T cells, but its expression on CD8+ T cells was unchanged by treatment and blocking it did not improve DSB1559 efficacy.
Intraductal Ad5CMVCre deletion of Brca1 with Trp53 in FVB/n mice generates the triple-negative mammary tumors used throughout.
Trp53 was co-deleted with Brca1 to produce tumors in the FVB/n model.

DSB1559 3 mg/kg oral daily produced tumor regression and significantly better overall survival than olaparib 50 mg/kg intraperitoneally over 60 days, n=11 to 12 per group, and no benefit in BRCA1 add-back tumors.
Human HSPC viability over 5 days was higher with DSB1559 than olaparib even at 10 micromolar, and higher than AZD5305 at top concentrations, n=3 donors; used as a toxicity surrogate.
Olaparib reduced HSPC viability more than the PARP1-selective agents, consistent with PARP2 inhibition driving hematologic toxicity.
Rat striatal microdialysis after a single 10 mg/kg oral dose detected DSB1559 by 30 minutes with unbound brain-to-plasma KPuu 0.3, exceeding niraparib, n=4 per group.
Niraparib, described as the most brain-penetrant approved PARP inhibitor, served as the microdialysis comparator and was exceeded by DSB1559.
DSB2455 is described as a structurally related PARP1-selective clinical lead now in phase Ia or Ib trial NCT06458712; no experimental data are shown for it here.
Intact homologous recombination protects cells from PARP1 inhibition; BRCA1 add-back restored resistance in KB1P and 904 models.
BRCA1-deficient triple-negative breast cancer is the clinical setting the model represents, and the authors note elevated CNS metastasis risk in BRCA carriers.
