papers.title: Senescent cancer-associated fibroblasts secrete Tenascin-C to promote tumor progression in high-grade serous ovarian cancer
papers.authors: Li R, Chen Y, Huang X, et al.

bibliographic.title: Senescent cancer-associated fibroblasts secrete Tenascin-C to promote tumor progression in high-grade serous ovarian cancer

reading.one_line_takeaway: In high-grade serous ovarian cancer the fibroblast compartment, especially myCAFs at metastatic sites, is the most senescent cell population, and NF-kB (p65/RELA) in these senescent CAFs transcriptionally drives Tenascin-C (TNC), which acts on tumor-cell SDC4 to switch on ERK and EMT and to accelerate growth and invasion.
reading.tldr: The authors asked how senescent cancer-associated fibroblasts (seneCAFs) promote HGSOC. Using the public HGSOC scRNA-seq atlas GSE165897 (10 primary, 4 metastatic tumors) plus an independent ascites-containing dataset (Zheng et al., Nat Cancer 2023), spatial data (GSE213699) and four bulk cohorts (TCGA-OV, GSE9891, GSE18520, GSE26712), they show CAFs carry the highest cellular senescence score of any cell type, that senescence is highest in myCAFs and in peritoneal and mesenteric metastases, and that a 54-gene seneCAF signature (reduced by LASSO Cox to 5 genes) predicts shorter overall survival. Conditioned medium from CAFs made senescent with H2O2 (200 uM, 4 h on two consecutive days) or with OVCAR3/SKOV3 tumor-conditioned medium increased OVCAR3 and SKOV3 proliferation, migration, invasion and EMT marker switching (Fig. 4). TNC was the only gene shared between the LASSO prognostic genes and the ligands upregulated in SeneHigh CAFs (Fig. 5A), was secreted at higher levels by seneCAFs by ELISA, and co-localized with p21+ aSMA+ fibroblasts in 8 HGSOC specimens. siRNA or shRNA knockdown of TNC abolished, and recombinant TNC (300 ng/mL) restored, the pro-tumor effect, which required tumor-cell SDC4 and ERK (Fig. 6), while p65 ChIP-seq in IMR-90 fibroblasts (GSE141992), ChIP-qPCR, the IKK inhibitor IKK16 (200 nM, 6 h) and p65 knockdown placed TNC downstream of NF-kB in seneCAFs (Fig. 7).
reading.research_question: Do cancer-associated fibroblasts in high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) acquire a senescent state, does that state carry prognostic information, and which secreted factor and receptor pathway lets senescent CAFs promote tumor cell proliferation, invasion and epithelial-mesenchymal transition?
reading.background: HGSOC is the most common and most aggressive ovarian cancer subtype, usually diagnosed late, treated with debulking surgery plus chemotherapy, and with five-year survival below 40 percent (the Background cites this to ref. 5). Cellular senescence, a stable cell cycle arrest marked by CDKN2A (p16) and CDKN1A (p21) upregulation, increased SA-beta-galactosidase activity and a senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP), is treated as a cancer hallmark that can remodel the microenvironment. Senescent CAFs had already been linked to progression in other tumors: IGF1 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, CTHRC1 in hepatocellular carcinoma, and impaired NK cell cytotoxicity in breast cancer. What was missing was (i) evidence that CAF senescence is a feature of HGSOC specifically, (ii) a transcriptomic definition of the HGSOC seneCAF state usable on bulk cohorts, and (iii) the effector molecule by which HGSOC seneCAFs act on tumor cells. Tenascin-C was already known as a pro-tumorigenic matrix glycoprotein with SDC4 among its receptors, but it had not been tied to the senescent CAF state.
reading.study_design: Computational layer: HGSOC scRNA-seq GSE165897 (primary tumor n=10, metastatic tumor n=4; the Results text at one point writes GSE165899, which looks like a typographical error) analyzed in Seurat v4.0.5, with seven annotated populations (epithelial, T, NK, myeloid, B, endothelial, CAF); an independent HGSOC scRNA-seq dataset (Zheng et al. 2023: primary n=10, metastatic n=4, ascites n=8, lymph node n=4, PBMC n=5) and a further recent HGSOC dataset on Mendeley Data as replication; spatial transcriptomics GSE213699 (HGSOC) and GSE225857 (CRC) with SingleR v2.4.0; bulk HGSOC cohorts TCGA-OV (training), GSE9891, GSE18520, GSE26712 (validation) with clinical annotation from curatedOvarianData v1.30.0; bulk CRC cohorts GSE17538 and GSE39582; CRC scRNA-seq GSE144735; pan-cancer TCGA via GDC; p65 ChIP-seq in IMR-90 fibroblasts GSE141992. Experimental layer: primary CAFs isolated from HGSOC specimens and previously characterized in the authors' own PNAS 2026 paper (ref. 16), human lines OVCAR3 and SKOV3, mouse L929 fibroblasts, mouse ID8 ovarian and MC38 colon lines, 293T for packaging. Senescence was induced either with H2O2 (200 uM, 4 h, two consecutive days) or with 4 days of tumor-conditioned medium (TCM) from OVCAR3 or SKOV3, and confirmed by p16/p21, SA-beta-Gal and EdU. Readouts used conditioned medium transfer (48 h in 5 percent FBS) or direct co-culture. Perturbations: siRNA against human TNC (2), human RELA/p65 (2), human SDC4 (2) and mouse Tnc; lentiviral shTNC in CAFs; IKK16 (NF-kB, 200 nM, 6 h); AZD8330 (MEK1/2); recombinant human TNC at 300 ng/mL. In vivo: female BALB/c nude mice, 5 weeks old, 5x10^6 OVCAR3 co-injected 1:1 with CAFs subcutaneously, 4 weeks, n=5 per group (Fig. 6 legend); female C57BL/6J mice with 1x10^7 ID8 or 2x10^6 MC38 cells and repeated conditioned-medium injection every 3 days. Human tissue: 8 treatment-naive FIGO stage IIIC HGSOC patients from Nanfang Hospital (ethics NFEC2024-630) for immunofluorescence. Statistics: GraphPad Prism 7.0.0 and R 4.1.2, mean plus or minus SEM, two-tailed Student t test for two groups, one-way or two-way ANOVA for more, Kaplan-Meier with log-rank, Pearson correlation in Fig. 5J, significance at p < 0.05, mostly n=3 independent replicates.

key_methods.name: Single-cell senescence scoring (Seurat AddModuleScore plus GSEA)
key_methods.plain_explanation: Single-cell RNA sequencing measures which genes are switched on in each individual cell, so a tumor can be split into its cell types. To ask how senescent a cell is, you take a predefined list of genes that go up when cells become senescent and give each cell an average expression score for that list, corrected against randomly chosen control genes of similar expression level (this is what Seurat's AddModuleScore does). Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) asks the same question a different way: it ranks all genes by how much higher they are in one group than another and tests whether the senescence genes sit near the top of that ranking.
key_methods.how_used: Applied to GSE165897 using the Gene Ontology cellular senescence set GO:0090398, plus FRIDMAN_SENESCENCE_UP and a SASP set from Gorgoulis et al. Scores were compared across the seven annotated cell types (Fig. 1F, G), across anatomical sites for CAFs only (Fig. 1H), and across the myCAF, iCAF and apCAF subtypes (Fig. 1I, J), with Wilcoxon rank-sum tests. The same comparisons were repeated in the Zheng et al. dataset (Additional file 2: Fig. S1C-G).
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the entire basis for the claim that CAFs, and myCAFs in particular, are the senescent compartment of HGSOC. The caveat is that a module score is a relative, library-size sensitive quantity: a cell type with high total RNA content or high ECM gene load can score higher without being arrested, and no orthogonal single-cell measure of arrest (for example lack of cycling phase assignment) is reported alongside it.

key_methods.name: seneCAF transcriptomic signature and LASSO Cox risk model
key_methods.plain_explanation: First a gene list that is specific to the senescent fibroblast state is built: CAFs are ranked by senescence score, the top and bottom quartiles are compared, and genes kept only if they are expressed in more than 25 percent of CAFs or SeneHigh CAFs and in fewer than 25 percent of all other cells, with log2 fold change above 0.25 and adjusted p below 0.05. LASSO Cox regression then takes that list into patient survival data and shrinks the coefficients of genes that add nothing to zero, so only a few genes with non-zero weights remain. Each patient gets a risk score that is the sum of gene expression times coefficient, and patients are split at the median.
key_methods.how_used: Filtering gave 54 candidate genes (Fig. 2C), whose aggregate score correlated with FAP, ACTA2, CDKN1A, CDKN2B and the senescence score but not with the epithelial marker EPCAM (Fig. 2D), and predicted shorter survival in TCGA-OV, GSE9891, GSE18520 and GSE26712 (Fig. 2E-H). LASSO Cox with glmnet v4.1-8, 10-fold cross-validation and minimum lambda in TCGA-OV reduced this to 5 genes (Fig. 3A, B). High risk predicted worse overall survival in TCGA-OV, GSE9891 and GSE26712 (Fig. 3D-F), with time-dependent AUCs at 1, 3 and 5 years of 0.567/0.607/0.651, 0.657/0.668/0.645 and 0.685/0.636/0.632 (Fig. 3G-I), and remained significant in multivariate Cox models (Fig. 3M-O). A nomogram added age and FIGO stage (Additional file 2: Fig. S6L, M).
key_methods.why_it_matters: It is what converts a single-cell cell-state observation into something testable on thousands of archived bulk tumors, and it is how TNC was nominated (TNC is one of the five LASSO genes). The caveat is that the AUC values, 0.57 to 0.69, are close to the range expected for a weak marker, the authors themselves concede limited standalone predictive power, and the five gene names and their coefficients are not stated in the text (they appear only inside Fig. 3A), which makes independent reimplementation impossible from the article body alone.

key_methods.name: CellChat ligand-receptor communication analysis
key_methods.plain_explanation: CellChat scores possible signaling between cell groups in single-cell data by combining the expression of a secreted ligand in the sending group with the expression of its known receptor (and co-receptors) in the receiving group, using a curated ligand-receptor database, and reports which pathways are strongest between which pairs of cell groups. It does not measure protein or any actual signaling event; it is an expression-based prediction.
key_methods.how_used: Run with CellChat v1.1.2 on GSE165897 after subclustering epithelial cells into ten subclusters (Additional file 2: Fig. S9A-D). Ligands preferentially expressed by SeneHigh CAFs were intersected with the five LASSO prognostic genes, and TNC was the single overlap (Fig. 5A). TNC signaling to epithelial subclusters was the top predicted interaction from SeneHigh CAFs (Fig. 5B), SDC4 was the main predicted receptor and was high in tumor cells (Additional file 2: Fig. S9I), and epithelial cells were then split into TNC-CrosstalkHigh and TNC-CrosstalkLow groups that differed in proliferation, migration and EMT pathway scores (Fig. 5C).
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the hypothesis-generating step that singled out TNC and SDC4 out of all possible SASP factors. Its weakness is that an intersection of two small gene lists is a fragile nomination procedure, and because TNC was already one of the five prognostic genes the overlap is not an independent line of evidence; the real support for TNC comes from the perturbation experiments in Fig. 6.

key_methods.name: In vitro induction of senescent CAFs plus conditioned medium transfer
key_methods.plain_explanation: Primary fibroblasts are pushed into senescence in a dish by either an acute oxidative insult (hydrogen peroxide, which causes DNA damage) or by prolonged exposure to medium that tumor cells have been growing in. The cells are then confirmed to be senescent by p16 and p21 levels, by the blue stain produced by senescence-associated beta-galactosidase, and by loss of DNA synthesis in an EdU incorporation assay. The medium those senescent fibroblasts secrete into is then collected and put onto tumor cells, so any effect must come from soluble or secreted material rather than from cell contact.
key_methods.how_used: H2O2 at 200 uM for 4 h on two consecutive days, or OVCAR3 or SKOV3 tumor-conditioned medium for 4 days with refreshment every 2 days. Senescence confirmed in Fig. 4A-F and Additional file 2: Fig. S8A-C. Conditioned medium (48 h in 5 percent FBS, centrifuged at 1000 g) was then applied to OVCAR3 (Fig. 4G-P) and SKOV3 (Additional file 2: Fig. S8D-M), with a direct co-culture arm as a control for the medium-transfer design (Fig. 4Q).
key_methods.why_it_matters: It provides the causal arm: senescent fibroblast secretions, not the tumor cells themselves, increase colony formation, EdU incorporation, wound closure, transwell migration and invasion, and shift E-cadherin down with N-cadherin and vimentin up. The caveat is model validity: 200 uM H2O2 is a strong acute oxidative stress that also damages many pathways besides senescence, and TCM-induced senescence is itself a composite stimulus, so neither is a clean genocopy of the spontaneous stromal senescence seen in patients.

key_methods.name: TNC, SDC4 and ERK epistasis: knockdown, rescue and pathway inhibition
key_methods.plain_explanation: To show that one molecule carries an effect, you remove it and ask whether the effect disappears, then add the purified molecule back and ask whether the effect returns, then remove the receptor or block the downstream kinase and ask whether the molecule still works. Small interfering RNA (siRNA) and shRNA destroy the messenger RNA of a chosen gene; recombinant protein supplies the molecule directly; a kinase inhibitor blocks the signaling step.
key_methods.how_used: Two siRNAs against TNC in CAFs (validated by qRT-PCR, Western blot and ELISA, Additional file 2: Fig. S11A-C) removed the pro-proliferative, pro-migratory and pro-invasive effect of seneCAF conditioned medium on OVCAR3 (Fig. 6A-D) and SKOV3 (Additional file 2: Fig. S13A-H), and lowered p-ERK and EMT markers (Fig. 6G, H). Recombinant human TNC at 300 ng/mL added back to knockdown medium restored all of it (Fig. 6I-K). Two SDC4 siRNAs in tumor cells abolished the TNC response (Additional file 2: Fig. S12G-J, Fig. S14A-D), and MEK1/2 inhibition with AZD8330 did the same (Additional file 2: Fig. S12K-M, Fig. S14E-G). Co-immunoprecipitation showed TNC and SDC4 binding (Additional file 2: Fig. S12E). Lentiviral shTNC CAFs were used in vivo (Fig. 6L-N).
key_methods.why_it_matters: This is the strongest evidence in the paper: loss, gain and receptor and kinase epistasis all line up, which makes the seneCAF-TNC-SDC4-ERK-EMT axis a genuine mechanistic claim rather than a correlation. The remaining gaps are that the ERK step is tested only with an inhibitor and not with a genetic MAPK1/MAPK3 perturbation, and that no TNC-neutralizing antibody was used, which the authors list as future work.

key_methods.name: NF-kB to TNC transcription: public p65 ChIP-seq plus ChIP-qPCR and inhibition
key_methods.plain_explanation: Chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) uses an antibody against a transcription factor to pull down the DNA that factor is sitting on. Sequencing all of that DNA (ChIP-seq) maps every binding site genome-wide; measuring one promoter by quantitative PCR (ChIP-qPCR) asks only whether binding at that site increased. Combining a public ChIP-seq map with a targeted ChIP-qPCR in the cells of interest tests whether a candidate factor binds a candidate promoter and whether that binding changes with treatment.
key_methods.how_used: KEGG enrichment of SeneHigh CAF genes in GSE165897 highlighted MAPK, PI3K-Akt, Hippo, TNF and NF-kB pathways (Fig. 7A), and NF-kB was the top activated pathway in TNC-high CAFs (Fig. 7B). H2O2 and TCM raised phospho-p65 in CAFs (Fig. 7C). Public p65 ChIP-seq in IMR-90 fibroblasts (GSE141992), viewed in IGV, showed a p65 peak at the TNC promoter against IgG (Fig. 7D), and ChIP-qPCR showed increased p65 occupancy at that promoter in H2O2-induced seneCAFs (Fig. 7E, F; n=3, Student t test). IKK16 at 200 nM for 6 h blocked the TNC increase (Fig. 7G-I), and RELA/p65 siRNA knockdown reduced TNC mRNA and protein (Fig. 7J-L, one-way ANOVA).
key_methods.why_it_matters: It supplies the upstream wiring, NF-kB as a direct transcriptional driver of TNC in senescent fibroblasts, which is the part most directly relevant to any NF-kB-centered stromal model. The caveat is that the genome-wide binding evidence comes from IMR-90 lung fibroblasts rather than from HGSOC CAFs, and that IKK16 blocks IKK and therefore has effects well beyond the TNC promoter.

key_concepts.plain_definition: Cellular senescence is a state in which a cell permanently stops dividing but stays alive and metabolically active, usually after DNA damage, telomere shortening, oxidative stress or oncogene activation. It is enforced by cell cycle inhibitor proteins, chiefly p16 encoded by CDKN2A and p21 encoded by CDKN1A, and it is recognized experimentally by that arrest, by raised senescence-associated beta-galactosidase activity, and by a changed secretion program. Senescence is double-edged: in a cell that is about to become cancerous it is protective, but a senescent cell sitting in a tumor's stroma keeps secreting and can help the tumor. In this paper senescence is scored in single cells (GO:0090398) and then induced on purpose in fibroblasts with H2O2 or tumor-conditioned medium, so that its consequences for tumor cells can be tested.

The SASP is the set of proteins a senescent cell secretes: inflammatory cytokines and chemokines such as IL6, CXCL1 and CXCL2, growth factors, proteases and matrix proteins. It is what makes senescence a condition of the neighborhood rather than of a single cell, because those factors act on epithelial, immune and endothelial cells nearby. The paper uses a published SASP gene set to score cells, finds SASP genes high in CAFs and endothelial cells (Additional file 2: Fig. S1B), and then argues that one matrix component of the SASP, Tenascin-C, is the functionally important one in HGSOC.

CAFs are the activated fibroblasts of a tumor's connective tissue. They are identified here by FAP and by ACTA2, the gene for alpha smooth muscle actin, and they shape tumors by laying down and remodeling extracellular matrix, by secreting cytokines and growth factors, and by suppressing immune attack. They are not one cell type: myofibroblastic CAFs (myCAFs) are contractile, matrix-producing cells usually found next to tumor cells, inflammatory CAFs (iCAFs) are cytokine-secreting cells usually further away, and antigen-presenting CAFs (apCAFs) express MHC class II. The paper's central cell-state claim is that of these three, myCAFs carry the highest senescence score in HGSOC (Fig. 1I, J).

Tenascin-C is a large extracellular matrix glycoprotein built from repeated modules, secreted rather than membrane-bound, and normally present during development, wound healing and inflammation but largely absent from healthy adult tissue. Because its different modules bind different partners, including integrins, fibronectin and the cell-surface proteoglycan SDC4, it can both change the physical matrix and act as a signaling ligand. It was already known as a poor-prognosis marker in several cancers; what is new here is its assignment to the senescent CAF state specifically, as the effector that carries the pro-tumor activity of seneCAF secretions in HGSOC.

SDC4 is a single-pass transmembrane heparan sulfate proteoglycan on the cell surface that works as a co-receptor: its sugar chains and core protein bind matrix molecules and growth factors and pass the signal inward, influencing focal adhesion, cytoskeletal organization and kinase cascades. In this paper SDC4 is the receptor through which TNC acts on HGSOC cells: it is predicted by CellChat, shown to bind TNC by co-immunoprecipitation, and required, because knocking it down in OVCAR3 and SKOV3 cells abolishes the TNC response.

ERK is the final kinase of the RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK cascade, one of the main routes by which signals from the cell surface reach the nucleus to turn on genes for proliferation, survival and motility. Activity is read out as phosphorylated ERK (p-ERK) on a Western blot, and it can be blocked upstream with a MEK1/2 inhibitor such as AZD8330. Here ERK is the intracellular step between the TNC-SDC4 interaction and the tumor cell's behavior: seneCAF medium raises p-ERK, TNC knockdown lowers it, recombinant TNC restores it, and MEK inhibition cancels the whole effect.

EMT is a reversible change of cell program in which an epithelial cell loosens its junctions with its neighbours, loses apical-basal polarity and takes on the motile, matrix-invading character of a mesenchymal cell. The standard molecular readout is a switch from E-cadherin, the junctional adhesion protein, toward N-cadherin and vimentin. In cancer it is associated with invasion, dissemination and treatment resistance rather than with a complete change of identity. This paper treats EMT as the tumor cell phenotype produced by seneCAF-derived TNC, both in vitro (Fig. 4O-Q, Fig. 6G, H, K) and in xenograft tissue by immunohistochemistry (Fig. 6N).

NF-kB is a family of transcription factors held inactive in the cytoplasm until the IKK kinase complex removes their inhibitor, after which they enter the nucleus and turn on inflammatory and stress-response genes. RELA, the p65 subunit, is the main activating member, and its phosphorylation is used as a marker of pathway activation. NF-kB is also the principal driver of the SASP, which is why it links senescence to secretion. In this paper NF-kB is the upstream switch: phospho-p65 rises in senescent CAFs, p65 occupies the TNC promoter, and either pharmacological IKK inhibition (IKK16) or RELA knockdown drops TNC.

HGSOC is the most common and most lethal histological type of ovarian cancer, now generally thought to originate in the fallopian tube epithelium rather than the ovarian surface, and characterized by near-universal TP53 mutation, widespread copy number change and frequent homologous recombination deficiency. It typically presents at an advanced stage with peritoneal spread and ascites, is treated with debulking surgery plus platinum-based chemotherapy, and relapses often, giving five-year survival below 40 percent. The paper's samples are all FIGO stage IIIC tumors, and much of the senescence signal comes from peritoneal and mesenteric metastatic sites rather than from the primary tumor.

key_concepts.term: LASSO Cox regression and a prognostic risk score
key_concepts.plain_definition: Cox regression relates gene expression to how long patients survive. When there are far more candidate genes than patients, LASSO (least absolute shrinkage and selection operator) adds a penalty that drives most coefficients exactly to zero, so the model keeps only a handful of genes and is less likely to be fitted to noise; the penalty strength is chosen by cross-validation. The surviving genes and their coefficients form a risk score, patients above the median are called high risk, and performance is judged by Kaplan-Meier separation and by the area under the time-dependent ROC curve (AUC), where 0.5 is a coin flip and 1.0 is perfect. Here the 54-gene seneCAF signature is reduced to 5 genes in TCGA-OV and tested in two independent cohorts, with AUCs of 0.57 to 0.69.

figures.label: Fig. 1
figures.title: CAFs are the most senescent compartment of HGSOC, with myCAFs and metastatic-site CAFs highest
figures.question: Is cellular senescence a feature of HGSOC CAFs specifically rather than of other cell types, and does it vary by anatomical site and CAF subtype?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A is the study schematic. Panel B is a t-SNE of GSE165897 colored by the seven annotated populations (epithelial, T, NK, myeloid, B, endothelial, CAF) with box plots of each population's proportion by tumor site. Panel C is KEGG enrichment of genes upregulated in CAFs. Panels D and E are GSEA running plots for the cellular senescence and SASP gene sets, CAFs against all other cells. Panel F projects the GO:0090398 AddModuleScore back onto the t-SNE as a color gradient, and panel G turns it into per-cell-type box plots (Wilcoxon rank-sum). Panel H is a violin plot of CAF senescence score split by anatomical site. Panels I and J repeat the score across myCAF, iCAF and apCAF. Panel K is immunofluorescence of patient tumor tissue, with aSMA and p21 double-positive cells marking seneCAFs, scale bar 200 um.
figures.key_result: CAFs carry a significantly higher senescence module score than the other six populations (Fig. 1F, G), and senescence and SASP gene sets are enriched in CAFs by GSEA (Fig. 1D, E). CAFs are more abundant in metastatic than primary lesions and CAFs from peritoneal and mesenteric metastases score higher than those from primary tumors (Fig. 1B, H). Among subtypes myCAFs score highest (Fig. 1I, J). Upregulated CAF genes are enriched for cellular senescence, HIF-1, NF-kB and ECM-receptor interaction (Fig. 1C). Within the atlas, CDKN2A is mainly epithelial whereas CDKN1A, IL6, CXCL1 and CXCL2 are high in CAFs and endothelial cells (Additional file 2: Fig. S1B). aSMA+ p21+ fibroblasts are present in patient HGSOC tissue (Fig. 1K). No p values are given in the text for these comparisons.

figures.label: Fig. 3
figures.title: Five-gene LASSO model from the seneCAF signature is an independent prognostic factor
figures.question: Can the seneCAF signature be compressed into a small gene model that predicts overall survival independently of age and stage?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A shows the genes LASSO retained, panel B their CAF-restricted expression as violin plots in GSE165897, panel C a univariate Cox forest plot with hazard ratios and confidence intervals. Panels D to F are Kaplan-Meier curves for high versus low risk in TCGA-OV (training), GSE9891 and GSE26712 (validation). Panels G to I are time-dependent ROC curves at 1, 3 and 5 years with AUCs. Panels J to L are univariate and M to O multivariate Cox analyses of the risk score together with clinical variables, after Z-score standardization of the score.
figures.key_result: LASSO Cox on the 54 candidate genes in TCGA-OV retained 5 genes, all CAF-specific in the single-cell data, each individually associated with worse prognosis (Fig. 3C and Additional file 2: Fig. S6D-H). High-risk patients had significantly shorter overall survival in all three cohorts (Fig. 3D-F). Time-dependent AUCs at 1, 3 and 5 years were 0.567, 0.607 and 0.651 in TCGA-OV; 0.657, 0.668 and 0.645 in GSE9891; and 0.685, 0.636 and 0.632 in GSE26712. The risk score stayed significant in multivariate models (Fig. 3M-O). Note that the five gene names and their coefficients are not stated in the article text; only TNC is identified later, in Fig. 5A.

figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.title: Secretions from senescent CAFs increase HGSOC cell proliferation, migration, invasion and EMT
figures.question: Do senescent CAFs act on tumor cells through soluble, secreted material, and is the effect specific to the senescent state rather than to CAFs in general?
figures.how_to_read: Panels A to C validate H2O2-induced senescence in CAFs (qRT-PCR and Western blot for p16 and p21; SA-beta-Gal staining; EdU to show the cells stopped dividing). Panels D to F do the same for OVCAR3 tumor-conditioned-medium-induced senescence. Panels G to J put conditioned medium from control or senescent CAFs onto OVCAR3 and measure colony formation (G, H) and EdU incorporation (I, J). Panels K to N measure motility: wound healing (K, L) and transwell migration and invasion (M, N). Panels O and P are Western blots for E-cadherin, N-cadherin and vimentin. Panel Q is immunofluorescence of EMT markers in EpCAM+ OVCAR3 cells after direct co-culture. All quantification is mean plus or minus SEM, n=3, Student t test; scale bars 200 um except transwell at 100 um.
figures.key_result: Both induction routes produced bona fide senescence: higher p16 and p21, more SA-beta-Gal, less EdU (Fig. 4A-F; SKOV3 TCM in Additional file 2: Fig. S8A-C). Conditioned medium from senescent CAFs, but not from control CAFs, increased OVCAR3 colony formation and EdU incorporation (Fig. 4G-J), wound closure (Fig. 4K, L) and transwell migration and invasion (Fig. 4M, N), and shifted the EMT markers (E-cadherin down, N-cadherin and vimentin up; Fig. 4O, P). Direct co-culture reproduced the marker shift (Fig. 4Q). All results were replicated in SKOV3 (Additional file 2: Fig. S8D-N).

figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.title: TNC is the seneCAF-secreted ligand nominated by both communication analysis and prognosis
figures.question: Which secreted factor of the senescent CAF state is the one acting on tumor cells, and is it actually made by senescent fibroblasts in patient tissue?
figures.how_to_read: Panel A is a Venn diagram intersecting the LASSO prognostic genes with ligands upregulated in SeneHigh CAFs. Panel B is the CellChat TNC signaling map between seneCAF subgroups and malignant cell populations. Panel C is GSVA of epithelial cells grouped by how much TNC crosstalk they receive. Panels D to F quantify TNC in H2O2-induced CAFs by qRT-PCR, Western blot and ELISA, and panels G to I repeat this for OVCAR3 TCM induction (mean plus or minus SEM, n=3, Student t test). Panel J is immunofluorescence in patient HGSOC tissue with a scatter plot of TNC mean fluorescence intensity against the fraction of aSMA+ cells that are p21+, scale bar 50 um, n=8, Pearson correlation.
figures.key_result: TNC was the single gene shared between the LASSO prognostic genes and the SeneHigh CAF ligands (Fig. 5A) and the top predicted ligand from SeneHigh CAFs to epithelial cells (Fig. 5B). Epithelial cells receiving high TNC crosstalk scored higher for proliferation, migration and EMT, while low-crosstalk cells were enriched for negative regulation of epithelial migration (Fig. 5C). TNC mRNA, protein and secreted protein all rose with both senescence inductions (Fig. 5D-I). In 8 treatment-naive FIGO IIIC HGSOC specimens, TNC co-localized with p21+ aSMA+ fibroblasts and TNC intensity correlated positively with the p21+ aSMA+ fraction, which averaged 42.5 percent of aSMA+ CAFs (range 20.3 to 75.7 percent) (Fig. 5J). SDC4, the predicted receptor, was high in tumor cells, and high TNC together with high SDC4 marked the worst outcomes (Additional file 2: Fig. S9I-K).

figures.label: Fig. 6
figures.title: seneCAF-derived TNC drives progression through tumor-cell SDC4 and ERK, in vitro and in xenografts
figures.question: Is TNC necessary and sufficient for the pro-tumor effect of senescent CAFs, and does it act through SDC4 and ERK?
figures.how_to_read: Panels A to D compare four conditions (control CAF medium, seneCAF medium, each with and without TNC knockdown) for EdU incorporation (A, B) and transwell migration and invasion (C, D), separately for H2O2 and TCM induction, analyzed by two-way ANOVA with n=3. Panel E is GO enrichment and panel F GSEA in SDC4-positive versus SDC4-negative epithelial cells from GSE165897. Panels G and H are Western blots of ERK phosphorylation and EMT markers. Panels I to K are the rescue arm: recombinant human TNC at 300 ng/mL added to knockdown medium, with EdU, transwell and Western readouts. Panels L and M show subcutaneous tumors and tumor weights in BALB/c nude mice co-injected with OVCAR3 and the various CAF preparations (n=5, two-way ANOVA, scale bar 1 cm), and panel N is immunohistochemistry of those tumors.
figures.key_result: TNC knockdown in seneCAFs removed the increase in OVCAR3 proliferation, migration and invasion (Fig. 6A-D) and lowered p-ERK and the EMT marker shift (Fig. 6G, H), and recombinant TNC at 300 ng/mL restored all of it (Fig. 6I-K). SDC4-positive tumor cells were enriched for epithelial proliferation, ERK signaling and EMT (Fig. 6E, F), TNC and SDC4 co-immunoprecipitated (Additional file 2: Fig. S12E), and knocking down SDC4 or inhibiting MEK1/2 abolished the TNC response (Additional file 2: Fig. S12G-M, Fig. S14A-G). In vivo, co-injection with H2O2- or TCM-induced seneCAFs increased tumor weight and TNC knockdown reduced it (Fig. 6L, M, n=5), with correspondingly higher TNC, Ki-67, p-ERK, N-cadherin and vimentin and lower E-cadherin by immunohistochemistry (Fig. 6N). A parallel syngeneic ID8 plus L929 experiment with intratumoral conditioned medium gave lower tumor weight and fewer Ki-67+ cells after Tnc knockdown (Additional file 2: Fig. S15E-I).

figures.label: Fig. 7
figures.title: NF-kB (p65/RELA) directly drives TNC transcription in senescent CAFs
figures.question: What turns TNC on when a CAF becomes senescent?
figures.how_to_read: Panels A and B are pathway enrichment in SeneHigh CAFs and in TNC-high CAFs from GSE165897. Panel C is a Western blot of total and phosphorylated p65 after H2O2, OVCAR3 TCM or SKOV3 TCM. Panel D is the p65 ChIP-seq track at the TNC promoter in IMR-90 fibroblasts (GSE141992) against an IgG control, viewed in IGV. Panels E and F are ChIP-qPCR and the corresponding agarose gel for p65 occupancy at the TNC promoter (n=3, Student t test). Panels G to I are Western blots of TNC and phospho-p65 after each induction with and without the IKK inhibitor IKK16 at 200 nM for 6 h. Panels J to L are qRT-PCR for RELA and TNC and a TNC Western blot after p65 knockdown (one-way ANOVA).
figures.key_result: SeneHigh CAFs were enriched for MAPK, PI3K-Akt, Hippo, TNF and NF-kB pathways (Fig. 7A), and NF-kB was the most activated pathway in TNC-high CAFs (Fig. 7B). All three senescence inductions raised phospho-p65 (Fig. 7C). Public p65 ChIP-seq showed a peak at the TNC promoter (Fig. 7D) and ChIP-qPCR showed significantly increased p65 occupancy there in H2O2-induced seneCAFs (Fig. 7E, F). IKK16 blocked the TNC increase (Fig. 7G-I) and RELA knockdown reduced TNC mRNA and protein (Fig. 7J-L).

key_findings.statement: Senescent CAFs act on HGSOC cells through secreted Tenascin-C, which binds tumor-cell SDC4 and activates ERK to drive EMT, proliferation, migration and invasion; TNC is both necessary and sufficient for this effect.
key_findings.evidence: TNC knockdown in seneCAFs removed the effect of their conditioned medium and lowered p-ERK and EMT markers in OVCAR3 and SKOV3 (Fig. 6A-D, G, H; Additional file 2: Fig. S13A-J); recombinant TNC at 300 ng/mL restored it (Fig. 6I-K); TNC and SDC4 co-immunoprecipitated (Additional file 2: Fig. S12E); SDC4 knockdown and MEK1/2 inhibition each abolished the response (Additional file 2: Fig. S12G-M, Fig. S14A-G); shTNC reduced tumor weight in OVCAR3 plus CAF xenografts (Fig. 6L, M, n=5) with matching immunohistochemistry (Fig. 6N).

key_findings.statement: NF-kB, acting through p65/RELA, is the transcriptional driver of TNC in senescent CAFs.
key_findings.evidence: Phospho-p65 rose with all three senescence inductions (Fig. 7C); public p65 ChIP-seq in IMR-90 fibroblasts showed a peak at the TNC promoter (Fig. 7D, GSE141992); ChIP-qPCR showed increased p65 occupancy in H2O2-induced seneCAFs (Fig. 7E, F); IKK16 at 200 nM blocked the TNC increase (Fig. 7G-I) and RELA siRNA reduced TNC mRNA and protein (Fig. 7J-L). NF-kB was also the top activated pathway in TNC-high CAFs in the single-cell data (Fig. 7B).

key_findings.statement: In HGSOC single-cell data, CAFs are the most senescent cell population, senescence is highest in myofibroblastic CAFs, and it is higher at peritoneal and mesenteric metastatic sites than in the primary tumor.
key_findings.evidence: AddModuleScore on GO:0090398 across seven populations in GSE165897 (Fig. 1F, G, Wilcoxon), GSEA for senescence and SASP sets (Fig. 1D, E), CAF score by site (Fig. 1H), score by myCAF/iCAF/apCAF (Fig. 1I, J), replicated in the Zheng et al. 2023 dataset (Additional file 2: Fig. S1C-G) and supported by FAP, ACTA2 and CDKN1A co-expression in spatial data GSE213699 (Additional file 2: Fig. S2A-E).

key_findings.statement: Senescent CAFs are abundant in patient HGSOC tissue, and the amount of TNC in a tumor tracks with how many of its CAFs are senescent.
key_findings.evidence: Immunofluorescence in 8 treatment-naive FIGO IIIC specimens: aSMA+ p21+ cells averaged 42.5 percent of aSMA+ CAFs (range 20.3 to 75.7 percent), TNC co-localized with them, and TNC mean fluorescence intensity correlated positively with the p21+ aSMA+ fraction by Pearson correlation (Fig. 1K, Fig. 5J). Spatial transcriptomics put TNC mainly in stromal regions (Additional file 2: Fig. S10A), consistent with Human Protein Atlas immunohistochemistry (Fig. S10B).

key_findings.statement: A 54-gene seneCAF transcriptomic signature, reduced by LASSO Cox to 5 genes including TNC, identifies HGSOC patients with shorter overall survival independently of age and FIGO stage, but with modest discrimination.
key_findings.evidence: Signature score separated survival in TCGA-OV, GSE9891, GSE18520 and GSE26712 (Fig. 2E-H) and correlated with FAP, ACTA2, CDKN1A, CDKN2B and the senescence score but not EPCAM (Fig. 2D). The 5-gene model separated survival in TCGA-OV, GSE9891 and GSE26712 (Fig. 3D-F) and stayed significant in multivariate Cox (Fig. 3M-O), but time-dependent AUCs were only 0.567 to 0.685 (Fig. 3G-I); the authors themselves note limited standalone predictive power and propose the nomogram with age and stage instead (Additional file 2: Fig. S6L, M).

key_findings.statement: Fibroblast senescence can be induced in two independent ways and in both cases makes the fibroblast secretome pro-tumorigenic, so the effect tracks the senescent state rather than CAF identity.
key_findings.evidence: H2O2 (200 uM, 4 h on two days) and 4-day OVCAR3 or SKOV3 tumor-conditioned medium both raised p16 and p21, increased SA-beta-Gal and reduced EdU in CAFs (Fig. 4A-F; Additional file 2: Fig. S8A-C), and conditioned medium from either preparation, but not from control CAFs, increased proliferation, motility and EMT markers in OVCAR3 and SKOV3 (Fig. 4G-Q; Fig. S8D-N).

key_findings.statement: High seneCAF risk score and high TNC are associated with worse overall survival across multiple solid tumors, and the TNC dependency is reproducible in colorectal cancer.
key_findings.evidence: Pan-cancer TCGA survival analyses (Additional file 2: Fig. S16A, C, E; Fig. S17A-F); in CRC (GSE17538, GSE39582, scRNA-seq GSE144735, spatial GSE225857) TNC and the risk score correlated with senescence score, tumor-border and tumor-region fibroblasts were more senescent than adjacent normal fibroblasts, TNC was the prognostic gene most specific to tumor-region fibroblasts, and Tnc knockdown in senescent fibroblasts slowed MC38 xenograft growth (Fig. S16B, D, F-N; Fig. S18A, B).

key_findings.statement: A high seneCAF risk score marks tumors with an EMT-high, angiogenic, matrix-remodeling program and a less favorable immune profile.
key_findings.evidence: Hallmark GSVA and GSEA in high-risk tumors showed mitotic spindle, hypoxia, EMT, angiogenesis and apical junction enrichment (Additional file 2: Fig. S7A-C); GO analysis showed cell adhesion and ECM processes (Fig. S7D); immune enrichment showed more regulatory T cells and fewer activated B cells, CD4+ and CD8+ T cells (Fig. S7E).

limitations: The senescence model is artificial in both arms. 200 uM H2O2 for 4 h on two consecutive days is an acute oxidative and DNA-damaging insult that alters far more than the senescence program, and 4 days of tumor-conditioned medium is a composite stimulus that may not produce the same state as the slowly accumulating stromal senescence seen in patient tissue. No deeply characterized alternative (replicative, oncogene-induced or therapy-induced senescence) is used as a comparator, and no transcriptomic comparison between the induced seneCAFs and the SeneHigh CAFs of GSE165897 is shown, so it is not established that the dish model reproduces the in vivo state the signature was derived from.

The prognostic model is weak as a classifier and under-reported. Time-dependent AUCs of 0.567 to 0.685 are in the range where a score adds little above stage; the authors acknowledge this. More importantly, the article text never names the five LASSO genes or gives their coefficients (they appear only inside Fig. 3A), and the 54 signature genes are given only as a Venn diagram (Fig. 2C), so the model cannot be reimplemented or independently validated from the paper body.

The in vivo work removes the immune system from the question. The main xenograft is OVCAR3 plus CAFs in BALB/c nude mice, which lack T cells, so the effect measured is tumor-cell-intrinsic; the authors state they did not examine the immunomodulatory effects of seneCAFs. This matters because the paper's own bulk analysis (Additional file 2: Fig. S7E) suggests an immune phenotype (more Tregs, fewer CD8+ T cells), and senescent CAFs in breast cancer were previously reported to act by impairing NK cytotoxicity. The syngeneic ID8 and MC38 experiments use mouse L929 fibroblast conditioned medium injected intratumorally rather than a genetic seneCAF model, so they test the ligand, not the stromal cell state in situ.

The causal chain is partly inferential at the receptor and kinase steps. SDC4 is nominated by CellChat and supported by co-immunoprecipitation and siRNA, but TNC has several receptors (integrins, other syndecans) that were not tested, so SDC4 may be necessary without being the only route. The ERK step rests on a single MEK1/2 inhibitor (AZD8330) with no genetic MAPK1/MAPK3 perturbation and no dose-response reported in the text. No TNC-neutralizing antibody was used, which the authors list as required future work before calling TNC a therapeutic target.

The human tissue evidence is small and correlational. Eight treatment-naive FIGO stage IIIC patients from a single hospital (Nanfang Hospital, NFEC2024-630), all one stage, support a within-tumor Pearson correlation between TNC intensity and the p21+ aSMA+ fraction (Fig. 5J) but cannot separate senescence from general CAF activation, and no non-malignant fallopian tube or ovarian stroma control is shown. The reported 42.5 percent mean p21+ aSMA+ fraction with a 20.3 to 75.7 percent range is a very wide spread for n=8, and p21 alone is a weak senescence marker (it also rises transiently with DNA damage and quiescence).

The single-cell senescence claim is methodologically fragile. It rests on a GO:0090398 module score compared across cell types, which is sensitive to library size, detection rate and the ECM and secretory gene load characteristic of fibroblasts; no orthogonal evidence of arrest in the CAF clusters (for example cell-cycle phase assignment, low MKI67, lamin B1 loss) is reported. The scRNA-seq Methods also omit QC thresholds, batch correction method, clustering resolution and the marker genes used for CAF and myCAF/iCAF/apCAF annotation, deferring the annotation to the authors' earlier paper (ref. 16), so the cell-state definitions cannot be checked.

Several internal inconsistencies should be checked against the version of record: the Results cite GSE165899 for the main scRNA-seq dataset where the Methods cite GSE165897; the Fig. 2D legend attributes the senescence score to ssGSEA while the Methods list only GSVA; the Results describe 21 days of intratumoral conditioned medium in the ID8 model while the Methods describe 4 weeks; and n is not stated in the Methods for the ID8 and MC38 experiments. The article is also an early-shared version subject to further edits.

Sender and receiver are not fully separated in the metastatic-site claim. CAFs were both more abundant and more senescent at peritoneal and mesenteric sites (Fig. 1B, H), which are also the sites with the most advanced disease, so site, tumor burden and fibroblast activation are confounded, and the cross-sectional single-cell data cannot say whether senescence precedes or follows metastatic colonization.

TNC is a known pan-cancer poor-prognosis matrix protein made by several cell types (the Discussion concedes tumor cells, stromal cells and vessels can all produce it). The claim that CAFs are the primary source in HGSOC rests on spatial and Human Protein Atlas localization plus in vitro secretion, not on a cell-type-specific genetic source experiment in vivo, so a tumor-cell contribution to the TNC pool is not excluded.
open_questions: Does the in vitro induced seneCAF transcriptome actually match the SeneHigh CAF state in patient tissue, and would bulk or single-cell RNA-seq of H2O2- and TCM-induced CAFs place them inside the 54-gene signature space?

Is the seneCAF-TNC axis an early event in HGSOC initiation or only a late feature of established peritoneal disease? Serous tubal intraepithelial carcinoma (STIC) and normal fallopian tube stroma were not examined, so the stage at which stromal senescence appears is unknown.

Which NF-kB-activating signal makes a CAF senescent in vivo? The paper shows NF-kB drives TNC once senescence exists but does not identify the upstream ligand (TNF, IL1, cGAS-STING-derived signaling from damaged tumor cells, or oxidative stress from ascites) in patient tissue.

Does the seneCAF-TNC axis also act on immune cells? Given more Tregs and fewer CD8+ T cells in high-risk tumors (Additional file 2: Fig. S7E) and the prior report of senescent CAFs impairing NK cytotoxicity in breast cancer, a syngeneic immunocompetent model with a stromal TNC deletion is the obvious next experiment.
Would a TNC-neutralizing antibody or an SDC4-blocking reagent reproduce the shTNC phenotype in vivo, and does senolytic clearance of seneCAFs do the same or better?
What are the other four LASSO genes, are they also secreted, and does the model still work when TNC is removed from it?
Is senescence of myCAFs mechanistically connected to the GREM1/FGFR1 myofibroblast program the same group reported in HGSOC (ref. 16), that is, are these the same cells at different times?
reading.relevance_to_lab: Relevance is to the lab's fallopian tube and HGSOC stroma arm (Chen, Han et al. 2026) rather than to the BRCA1 breast work, and it is partial but real. Where it extends the lab model: the lab's model has stromal ERalpha controlling an ECM-plus-cytokine output (POSTN, FGF1/FGF2, TNF, IL1, CCL2) that sets epithelial state, with estrogen excess pushing the stroma into an inflammatory, NF-kB-active condition that favors a progenitor-like epithelium. This paper independently arrives at NF-kB-active fibroblasts whose ECM output (TNC) reprograms the epithelium, and it supplies the receptor and kinase that the lab's model currently lacks on the epithelial side: TNC binds SDC4 and activates ERK to push an EMT and progenitor-like, migratory program (Fig. 5C, Fig. 6E-K). TNC sits in the same functional class as POSTN (both are NF-kB-inducible, fibroblast-derived matricellular proteins that signal to epithelium), so a concrete test is whether stromal ERalpha loss or estrogen excess in the lab's mouse fallopian tube changes TNC and SDC4 alongside POSTN, and whether POSTN and TNC are co-regulated in the lab's fibroblast subtypes. The paper also adds a mechanism for the lab's aging-stroma observation: it reports CDKN1A, IL6, CXCL1 and CXCL2 high in CAFs and endothelium (Additional file 2: Fig. S1B) and SeneHigh CAFs defined partly by CDKN2A, CDKN1A, CDKN2B, CXCL1 and CXCL2 (Fig. 2B). The lab's aging fallopian tube stroma shows more CCL2, CXCL1 and CXCL2, so stromal senescence is a plausible unifying explanation for the lab's aging phenotype, and the lab can score its own aged versus young stroma with GO:0090398, FRIDMAN_SENESCENCE_UP and the Gorgoulis SASP set, which are the three sets used here. Where it does not support the lab model: ESR1, estrogen, estrogen receptor and hormone do not appear anywhere in the paper, and neither do POSTN, CCL2, IL1B, PI16, SFRP4 or fallopian tube. TNF appears only as one enriched KEGG term in Fig. 7A. So the paper is silent on the hormonal input that the lab's model places upstream, and the senescence it describes is in established stage IIIC metastatic disease, not in pre-neoplastic tube. The paper therefore neither confirms nor challenges the estrogen arm; it supplies a parallel, hormone-independent route to an NF-kB-active, ECM-secreting stroma. Reusable material for the lab's GSE151214 human fallopian tube analysis: (1) the three senescence and SASP gene sets above, applied to Fib_PI16_C7, Fib_SFRP4_OGN and Fib_POSTN_ESR1hi to ask which subtype is most senescent, with the specific prediction from this paper that the myofibroblastic, matrix-producing subtype (the lab's Fib_POSTN_ESR1hi is the closest analogue to a myCAF) should score highest; (2) TNC, SDC4 and CDKN1A as genes to add to the lab's fibroblast and epithelial marker panels, and the aSMA plus p21 double immunofluorescence protocol used in Fig. 1K and Fig. 5J for tube and STIC sections; (3) the datasets themselves, which the lab does not currently use and which are directly comparable to its HGSOC interest: scRNA-seq GSE165897 (10 primary, 4 metastatic HGSOC) and the Zheng et al. 2023 ascites dataset, spatial transcriptomics GSE213699, bulk cohorts GSE9891, GSE18520 and GSE26712 with curatedOvarianData clinical annotation, and p65 ChIP-seq GSE141992 in IMR-90 fibroblasts, which the lab could use to ask whether NF-kB binds the promoters of its own stromal ERalpha target genes including POSTN, CCL2 and IL6; (4) the CellChat plus LASSO Cox pipeline as a template for turning the lab's fibroblast subtypes into a prognostic ligand nomination in TCGA-OV. There is also a thread back to the lab's BRCA1 work: the common node is NF-kB. In the breast model NF-kB is downstream of BRCA1 loss via cytosolic DNA and cGAS-STING and reshapes the SASP and immune surveillance; here NF-kB in the stroma writes an ECM output. Whether BRCA1- or TP53-deficient tube epithelium triggers NF-kB-dependent senescence in neighboring fibroblasts is an experiment the lab is unusually well placed to do, and this paper supplies the readouts.
discussion_questions: The lab's model routes stromal effects on fallopian tube epithelium through ERalpha and POSTN; this paper routes them through NF-kB and TNC with no hormonal input at all. Are these two branches of one stromal program, and would measuring TNC and SDC4 in the lab's stromal Esr1 knockout and estrogen-excess mice settle it?

Is the senescence signal here a cell state or an artifact of scoring fibroblasts? The claim rests on a GO:0090398 module score with no orthogonal arrest measure, and the patient-tissue marker is p21 alone. What would convince us: lamin B1 loss, cell-cycle phase assignment in GSE165897, or a p16 reporter?

myCAFs are the most senescent subtype here, and the same group previously described GREM1/FGFR1 myofibroblasts in HGSOC. If the lab scores senescence in its own Fib_PI16_C7, Fib_SFRP4_OGN and Fib_POSTN_ESR1hi subtypes in GSE151214, which should be highest, and does the aging tube phenotype (more CCL2, CXCL1, CXCL2) actually resolve into one senescent subtype or spread across all three?

All of the senescence here is in stage IIIC metastatic disease. Does stromal senescence exist in normal fallopian tube and in STIC lesions, and if it does, is it a driver of initiation (the lab's question) or a consequence of an established tumor (this paper's setting)?

The xenograft is in nude mice and the authors explicitly set the immune question aside, yet their own bulk data show more Tregs and fewer CD8+ T cells in high-risk tumors, and senescent CAFs were reported to impair NK cytotoxicity in breast cancer. Does TNC act on immune cells too, and is this the bridge between the lab's NK surveillance work and its stroma work?

nodes.label: Senescent CAFs promote other cancers; HGSOC role unknown
nodes.detail: Senescent CAFs had been linked to progression via IGF1 in esophageal cancer, CTHRC1 in liver cancer and impaired NK cytotoxicity in breast cancer, but CAF senescence had not been defined in HGSOC, whose five-year survival is below 40 percent.

nodes.label: Are HGSOC CAFs senescent, and what do they secrete?
nodes.detail: The paper asks whether CAF senescence is a feature of HGSOC, whether it carries prognostic information, and which secreted factor and receptor pathway lets senescent CAFs act on tumor cells.

nodes.label: Senescent CAFs secrete a factor that drives HGSOC progression
nodes.detail: Hypothesis: HGSOC CAFs acquire a senescent state whose secretory output acts on tumor cells to promote proliferation, invasion and EMT.

nodes.label: scRNA-seq, spatial, four bulk cohorts, cell and mouse models
nodes.detail: GSE165897 plus an independent ascites dataset and spatial GSE213699; bulk TCGA-OV, GSE9891, GSE18520, GSE26712; primary CAFs made senescent with H2O2 or tumor-conditioned medium; OVCAR3 and SKOV3; nude-mouse co-injection; CRC datasets and MC38 for generalization.

nodes.label: CAFs are the most senescent cells; myCAFs and metastatic sites highest
nodes.detail: GO:0090398 module score and GSEA put CAFs above the six other populations, with the highest scores in myCAFs and in peritoneal and mesenteric metastases; aSMA+ p21+ cells are present in patient tissue.

nodes.label: 54-gene seneCAF signature predicts poor survival in four cohorts
nodes.detail: SeneHigh versus SeneLow CAF comparison with strict cell-specificity filters gave 54 genes whose score tracked FAP, ACTA2, CDKN1A and CDKN2B but not EPCAM, and predicted shorter survival in TCGA-OV, GSE9891, GSE18520 and GSE26712.

nodes.label: Five-gene LASSO model independent but weak, AUC 0.57 to 0.69
nodes.detail: LASSO Cox in TCGA-OV kept five CAF-specific genes; high risk predicted worse survival in three cohorts and stayed significant in multivariate Cox, but time-dependent AUCs were only 0.567 to 0.685.

nodes.label: seneCAF secretions drive proliferation, migration and EMT
nodes.detail: Conditioned medium from H2O2- or TCM-induced seneCAFs, but not from control CAFs, increased OVCAR3 and SKOV3 colony formation, EdU, wound closure, transwell migration and invasion, and shifted E-cadherin down with N-cadherin and vimentin up.

nodes.label: TNC is the seneCAF ligand nominated and seen in patient tissue
nodes.detail: TNC was the only overlap between LASSO prognostic genes and SeneHigh CAF ligands and the top predicted CellChat ligand to epithelium; TNC mRNA, protein and secretion rose in seneCAFs and TNC intensity correlated with the p21+ aSMA+ CAF fraction in 8 patients.

nodes.label: TNC acts through tumor-cell SDC4 and ERK, in vitro and in vivo
nodes.detail: TNC knockdown abolished and recombinant TNC at 300 ng/mL restored proliferation, invasion, p-ERK and EMT markers; SDC4 knockdown and MEK1/2 inhibition each blocked the response; shTNC reduced xenograft weight with matching immunohistochemistry.

nodes.label: p65 binds the TNC promoter and NF-kB inhibition lowers TNC
nodes.detail: Phospho-p65 rose with all senescence inductions; public IMR-90 p65 ChIP-seq showed a TNC promoter peak and ChIP-qPCR showed increased occupancy in seneCAFs; IKK16 and RELA knockdown both reduced TNC.

nodes.label: Risk score and TNC are prognostic pan-cancer; CRC reproduces it
nodes.detail: High risk score and high TNC marked worse survival across solid tumors; in CRC, tumor-region fibroblasts were most senescent, TNC was the most tumor-fibroblast-specific prognostic gene, and Tnc knockdown slowed MC38 xenograft growth.

nodes.label: NF-kB-driven seneCAFs secrete TNC acting on SDC4-ERK to drive EMT
nodes.detail: The paper concludes that senescent CAFs in HGSOC activate NF-kB, which transcribes TNC, and that secreted TNC engages tumor-cell SDC4 and ERK to induce EMT and progression.

nodes.label: seneCAF signature is a prognostic but modest HGSOC biomarker
nodes.detail: The signature and its five-gene reduction are independently prognostic across cohorts, but the authors concede limited standalone discrimination and propose combining it with age and stage in a nomogram, with prospective validation still needed.

nodes.label: TNC blockade as a stromal target in HGSOC and other solid tumors
nodes.detail: Because TNC loss abolished the seneCAF effect in both HGSOC and CRC models, the authors propose TNC as a therapeutic target, while noting that neutralizing antibodies still have to be developed and tested.

nodes.label: Immune arm of the seneCAF axis remains untested
nodes.detail: High risk score tumors showed more regulatory T cells and fewer CD8+ T cells (Additional file 2: Fig. S7E), yet the authors state they did not examine the immunomodulatory effects of seneCAFs and the nude-mouse model excludes T cells.
